item.title: Amit: Political parties must show patience and tolerance to fulfil July aspirations
item.description:
State Minister for Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Anindya Islam Amit on Wednesday said all political parties must exercise patience and tolerance to realise the aspirations of the July movement, stressing that democratic values should be reflected in both words and actions.
Speaking to reporters after a rally and wreath-laying ceremony marking July Mass Uprising Day in Jessore, Amit said the government remains committed to safeguarding human rights, ensuring good governance and protecting freedom of expression.
"To fulfil the aspirations of July, every political party must act with patience and tolerance," he said. "If we use the same rhetoric that the fascists once used, it would show that we have not truly embraced democracy. Political ideologies may differ, but at the end of the day, our shared goal is to build a modern, self-reliant Bangladesh."
Earlier, a colorful procession began at 10:30 am from the premises of the Deputy Commissioner's Office and marched through the town's main roads before concluding at the Martyrs’ Memorial at Bakultala.

DU inaugurates foundation of July Memorial Monument
item.description:
Dhaka University on Wednesday inaugurated the foundation of the July Memorial Monument, which is being built in memory of those killed during the July 2024 mass uprising.
Dhaka University Vice-Chancellor Prof ABM Obaidul Islam inaugurated the project at a ceremony held on the campus.
Among those present were the fathers of martyrs Mir Mughdo, Faiyaz and Yamin, along with the university's Pro-Vice-Chancellors (Academic and Administration), Treasurer, deans of different faculties, the proctor, teachers and university officials.
Speaking at the programme, the vice-chancellor said: "Two years ago today, a new sun rose over Bangladesh through the mass uprising that began on July 1 and culminated on what protesters referred to as '36 July,' or August 5. Sheikh Hasina fled the country with her sister. We have achieved a new Bangladesh through the blood of the martyrs."
He paid tribute to those killed and injured during the uprising and prayed for the eternal peace of the departed souls.
"To preserve the memory of the martyrs of the uprising, we are establishing the July Memorial Monument," he said.
Prof Obaidul alleged that, over the past 17 years, the Awami League government had committed various injustices to consolidate its power while ignoring the will and demands of the people.
"We cannot measure the extent to which people were indiscriminately killed and shot in their own country. There can be no forgiveness for such acts," he said.
The vice-chancellor also said the university had not forgotten what he described as the suppression of dissent under the previous Dhaka University administration.
"We have not forgotten the persecution of dissenting voices," he said, expressing hope that "fascism will never return to this country on the blood of the martyrs."

item.title: Ziaur Rahman killing case: Prosecution seeks Facebook data of Mozaffar
item.description:
The prosecution has written to Meta seeking the Facebook and Messenger data of former army officer Md Mozaffar Hossain, who was arrested over allegations of involvement in the killing of late president Ziaur Rahman.
International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) Prosecutor and IT expert Tanvir Hasan Zoha confirmed the matter to Dhaka Tribune on Wednesday.
According to the prosecution, the request was made after investigators found evidence that Mozaffar had communicated directly with several individuals through Messenger and maintained contact with certain groups. Efforts are also underway to recover his deleted Messenger conversations.
Zoha said the information has been sought to assist the tribunal's ongoing investigation into crimes against humanity.
The prosecution has requested subscriber information, account registration details, all current and previously registered email addresses and phone numbers, complete login history with timestamps, IP addresses and devices used to access the account, browser information, and all Facebook Messenger data, including deleted conversations.
Ziaur Rahman, founder of the BNP and the country's then president, was killed during a military uprising in Chittagong on May 30, 1981.
Investigators allege that former army officer Mozaffar Hossain played a role in the disappearance of Ziaur Rahman's body after the killing. At the time, he held the rank of major in the Bangladesh Army. He went into hiding following the incident, and authorities announced a reward for information leading to his arrest.
After remaining a fugitive for 45 years, he was arrested by Detective Branch (DB) police from Banani in Dhaka on the night of July 15 and was subsequently handed over to the Bangladesh Army.
On July 23, ICT-2 ordered that Mozaffar be shown arrested in a crimes against humanity case linked to the July Mass Uprising. The tribunal also granted investigators two days to interrogate him and directed that he remain in army custody.
Earlier, ICT Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam said investigators had found evidence of regular communication between Mozaffar and retired lieutenant general Masud Uddin Chowdhury.
According to the chief prosecutor, Masud was one of the influential figures in the army-backed caretaker government in 2007 and is currently in custody in a crimes against humanity case. Mozaffar has also been shown arrested in the same case.
Aminul Islam said Mozaffar's trial over the killing of Ziaur Rahman would proceed under military law and is separate from the ICT proceedings.
"Our investigation concerns crimes against humanity. We will examine whether he had any involvement during the Awami League government's 16 years in power. Our judicial process is completely separate," he said.
He added that Mozaffar would remain in army custody and be brought before ICT investigators for questioning whenever necessary. If the allegations are established, he will face trial under the tribunal's applicable laws.

item.title: Land minister: Govt to stand by families of July martyrs, injured
item.description:
Land Minister Mizanur Rahman Minu on Wednesday said the government will continue to stand by the families of the July mass uprising martyrs and the injured, ensuring their treatment, welfare and long-term rehabilitation.
"The government is committed to upholding the sacrifices of the martyrs and the spirit of the student-people's movement against fascism," he told journalists after placing wreaths at the July Memorial Monument at C&B Intersections.
He said plans are underway to ensure long-term financial security for the martyrs' families and reiterated the government's commitment to building a prosperous and discrimination-free Bangladesh in line with the aspirations of the July mass uprising.
Earlier, the minister paid tribute to the martyrs by laying wreaths at the memorial alongside senior officials of the divisional and district administration.
Among those present were Rajshahi Divisional Commissioner A N M Bazlur Rashid, Rajshahi City Corporation Administrator Md Mahfuzur Rahman Riton, Rajshahi Metropolitan Police Commissioner Mohammad Foyzul Kabir, Rajshahi Deputy Commissioner Kazi Shahidul Islam and Rajshahi Zila Parishad Administrator Advocate Ershad Ali Isha.

item.title: 10 injured in clash between Chhatra Dal, Shibir activists at Barisal University
item.description:
At least 10 people were injured in a clash between activists of Chhatra Dal and Chhatra Shibir at Barisal University on Wednesday over allegations that outsiders had joined a campus rally.
The clash broke out in the morning when the university unit of Chhatra Shibir brought out a procession titled "Indomitable July," according to witnesses and campus sources.
An argument reportedly began after Chhatra Dal activists objected to the alleged presence of outsiders in the rally. The altercation later escalated into a clash, followed by several rounds of chase and counter-chase.
Ashiq Ahmed, senior vice-president of the university unit of Chhatra Dal, alleged that Chhatra Shibir had entered the campus with outsiders carrying sticks and flags.
He claimed that Shibir activists attacked Chhatra Dal members after they requested that the programme be held without outsiders, leaving five to six of their activists injured.
Rejecting the allegation, Zakaria Islam Babu, general secretary of the university unit of Chhatra Shibir, said they had been holding a peaceful program marking the anniversary of the July Uprising when Chhatra Dal activists attacked them near the vice-chancellor's gate.
He claimed that around five Shibir activists were injured in the attack and alleged that the incident occurred in the presence of university authorities. Although the university proctor tried to control the situation, the attack continued, he added.
Zakaria also said a complaint had been submitted to the university's vice-chancellor seeking justice over the incident.
Both student organisations blamed each other for triggering the violence.
The university proctor could not be reached for comment.
Belal Hossain, additional deputy commissioner of Barisal Metropolitan Police, said police rushed to the campus after receiving information about the clash.
"Additional police have been deployed on the campus following the incident. We have urged both sides to remain calm," he said.
Earlier on Tuesday, violence erupted as activists of Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal (JCD) and Bangladesh Islami Chhatra Shibir clashed at several educational institutions in the capital, leaving dozens injured.

item.title: State July celebration disrupted over documentary controversy
item.description:
A state ceremony marking the second anniversary of the July Mass Uprising descended into protests on Wednesday after audience members accused the government of distorting the movement’s history through an official documentary, forcing ministers to apologise and promise immediate corrections.
The unprecedented disruption unfolded in the presence of Acting President Hafiz Uddin Ahmed Bir Bikram at the Bangladesh-China Friendship Conference Center, where families of July martyrs, injured protesters, students and political activists interrupted the program with chants of “Fake, fake” after the documentary was screened.
The protest briefly threw the nationally televised event into disorder, prompting members of the acting president’s security detail to take positions on the stage and inside the auditorium while several invited foreign guests left the venue amid the commotion.
The controversy centred on allegations that the documentary failed to accurately portray the July uprising, omitted key developments -- particularly the events of August 3 -- and inadequately reflected the sacrifices of protesters and the movement’s leadership.
As slogans echoed through the auditorium, organisers repeatedly appealed for calm, but the protest continued.
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed eventually addressed the gathering, inviting protesters to speak from the stage and urging them to remain seated.
Seeking to defuse tensions, he requested National Citizen Party (NCP) Member Secretary Akhtar Hossain to address the audience.
Akhtar acknowledged the concerns raised by protesters, saying the documentary contained “inconsistencies” that required correction.
“We have also seen the inconsistencies in the documentary,” he said.
“The events of August 3 are completely absent. We will raise these issues with the government and seek accountability from the ministry. But on this historic day, we must remain calm out of respect for the families of the martyrs.”
Following his appeal, Akhtar and other NCP leaders left the venue after taking permission from the acting president.
As protests continued, Liberation War Affairs Minister Ahmed Aazam Khan returned to the stage and publicly apologised to the audience.
“Today’s documentary has caused you pain,” he said.
“The July movement and the mass uprising belong to all of us. We will carefully review every inconsistency, including the omission of the events of August 3, and take immediate steps to correct them.”
He also assured the audience that the documentary would be reviewed in consultation with representatives of the martyrs’ families and injured July fighters before being revised.
Only after the minister’s apology and commitment to amend the film did the protesters withdraw their objections, allowing the remainder of the program to proceed.
The event, organised by the Ministry of Liberation War Affairs, began with a reception for the families of July martyrs and injured July fighters before the documentary was shown.

item.title: Swapon calls for equitable, accountable state inspired by July Uprising
item.description:
Information and Broadcasting Minister Zahir Uddin Swapon on Wednesday called on all to work together to build an equitable, accountable and humane state inspired by the spirit of the July Mass Uprising.
Speaking at a discussion and reception for families of the July martyrs at the District Shilpakala Academy auditorium in Barishal, organized to mark July Mass Uprising Day 2026, the minister said the ideals of the historic movement must remain alive in the hearts of every citizen.
He said the spirit forged through the sacrifices and aspirations of thousands of people must not be undermined by any force, urging everyone to remain united and vigilant.
Swapon said that a group and a single family had monopolised democracy and people's rights for years, weakening democratic institutions and depriving citizens of their voting rights.
He urged people from all walks of life, regardless of political affiliation, religion or ethnicity, to forge unity to protect democracy.
The minister said attempts had been made to divide people through intimidation, greed and promises of power, but conscious citizens rejected such temptations and prioritised the country's interests.
He emphasized that the July Mass Uprising was not the work of a few individuals but a collective resistance against prolonged deprivation, injustice and oppression.
The strength of this movement is laying in the unity, courage and unwavering faith of the people in democracy, he said.
Barisal Divisional Commissioner Khalil Ahmed chaired the program, where government officials, political leaders, media representatives and families of the July martyrs were present.
A documentary on the July martyrs was also screened.

item.title: Sand-laden trucks outside Khaleda Zia's residence: Ex-joint secretary sent to jail
item.description:
A Dhaka court on Wednesday sent former joint secretary Syed Jaglul Pasha to jail in a case over allegations that he helped obstruct former prime minister Khaleda Zia from attending a political rally in 2013 by barricading the road outside her Gulshan residence with sand-laden trucks and using pepper spray.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Kamal Uddin passed the order after Gulshan Zonal Team Inspector Anwar Hossain produced Jaglul Pasha before the court and sought a 10-day remand. The court fixed Thursday for the remand hearing. SI Mokhtar Hossain of the prosecution confirmed the matter
Jaglul was arrested by the Dhaka Metropolitan Police's Detective Branch (DB) from his Bashundhara residence at around 1:30am on Tuesday.
According to the case statement, Jaglul was among 111 named accused, along with 250-300 unidentified individuals, who allegedly gathered outside Khaleda Zia's Gulshan residence on December 28, 2013, armed with deadly weapons. They allegedly remained there throughout the day, assaulted BNP leaders and activists, carried out acts of sabotage by blocking roads, and created obstacles to prevent Khaleda Zia from attending a scheduled political rally.
The complaint further alleged that at around 9am on December 29, 2013, when Khaleda Zia was preparing to leave for the rally with her entourage, the accused barricaded the road with sand-laden trucks and other vehicles. Despite repeated attempts to leave, they allegedly prevented her movement and used banned pepper spray with the intent to kill, leaving Khaleda Zia and several leaders and activists accompanying her injured.
The case was filed at Gulshan Police Station in October 2024 by Shariful Islam Shawon, former joint secretary of the Latif Hall unit of Rajshahi University Chhatra Dal.
Jaglul Pasha also faces allegations in the Zia Orphanage Trust case of preparing forged documents and giving false testimony before the court in proceedings involving former prime minister Khaleda Zia.

item.title: Three everyday kitchen items that could be harming your health
item.description:
Some everyday kitchen items—including old sponges, damaged non-stick pans, and dishwashing liquids with harsh chemicals—can pose hidden health risks if they are not used or replaced properly. Experts say simple changes in your kitchen routine can help reduce the risk of foodborne illness and unnecessary chemical exposure.
Old kitchen sponge
Kitchen sponges stay damp for long periods, making them an ideal breeding ground for bacteria and fungi. Over time, they can harbor harmful bacteria such as Salmonella and E. coli . These microbes can contaminate dishes and food, increasing the risk of foodborne illness, including diarrhea, vomiting, stomach infections, and fever.
When to replace it:
Dishwashing liquid with harsh chemicals
Some dishwashing liquids contain artificial fragrances, dyes, and other chemicals that may cause irritation in sensitive individuals. If dishes are not rinsed thoroughly, small amounts of residue may remain on the surface. In some people, this may contribute to skin irritation, dermatitis, eye irritation, or respiratory discomfort.
How to use it safely:
Damaged non-stick pan
A non-stick pan with deep scratches or a peeling coating should be replaced. Tiny particles from the damaged coating may end up in food, while overheating worn non-stick cookware can release fumes that may irritate the eyes and throat and cause temporary flu-like symptoms known as polymer fume fever.
Experts also recommend avoiding overheating non-stick cookware and considering alternatives such as stainless steel, cast iron, or tri-ply cookware.
Safe cookware practices:
Small changes can make a big difference
These kitchen items are not inherently dangerous, but improper use or failure to replace them regularly can increase health risks. Simple habits—such as replacing your sponge regularly, choosing gentler cleaning products, and discarding damaged cookware—can help reduce the risk of foodborne illness and unnecessary exposure to potentially harmful substances.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 854 as five die in 24 hours
item.description:
Five more children have died from measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am on Wednesday, raising the overall death toll from the ongoing outbreak to 854.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified all five of the latest casualties as suspected.
With the latest figures, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 758, while the number of confirmed deaths remained unchanged at 96, as no new confirmed measles deaths were reported in the last 24 hours.
Among the five new suspected fatalities, the highest concentration was recorded in Dhaka, with three deaths reported in both the Dhaka division and Dhaka district.
A total of 959 suspected measles cases were recorded in the 24 hours till Wednesday morning, taking the overall suspected case tally to 132,905.
During the same period, 124 new confirmed measles cases were reported, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 16,655.
Since March 15, 2026, a total of 115,234 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 111,005 have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, according to the DGHS.

Azam Khan: Govt to implement July Charter in spirit of July Uprising
item.description:
Liberation War Affairs Minister Ahmed Azam Khan on wednesday said the government would implement the July Charter in the spirit of the July Uprising, expressing optimism that the movement had paved the way for a prosperous and democratic Bangladesh.
"We will implement the July Charter in the spirit of the July Uprising. People now want prosperity and democracy. We believe that the uprising has brought about a significant transformation," he said.
The minister made the remarks after laying a wreath at the July Martyr Memorial in Shahbagh this morning on the occasion of July Mass Uprising Day.
Azam Khan said the uprising was not merely a mass movement but the beginning of a new chapter of political and institutional reforms.
He said the elected government, led by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman had begun the journey of rebuilding the country by drawing inspiration from the spirit of the uprising.
"Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has started the journey of rebuilding the country alongside the entire nation. He also tirelessly guided the July Mass Uprising," the minister said.
Referring to the political background of the uprising, Azam Khan said it was the outcome of an 18-year struggle by political parties, including the BNP, together with students and people from all walks of life.
He called on all political parties and leaders to preserve national unity.
"I request everyone not to divide the nation over narrow personal interests. The people have united for a prosperous and democratic country. If anyone tries to behave like the fallen fascist regime and divide the nation again, the public will not accept it," he said.
The minister also said freedom of speech had been restored and that the government, under the leadership of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, would continue working to build a prosperous Bangladesh.

item.description: Former chief adviser of the interim government, Professor Muhammad Yunus, on Wednesday said the July Memorial Museum is not just an establishment but the beginning of a new chapter in Bangladesh's history. "The path of a new Bangladesh will begin from here. If we lose our way, we will start from here," he said while speaking at the inauguration ceremony of July Memorial Museum in Dhaka. "If we ever lose our way in the future, the journey of a new Bangladesh will start from the museum again," he said. Prof Yunus asked the youth of the country to be the writers of this memory and come forward towards creating a new Bangladesh. At the end of the program, Prof Yunus urged all present there to visit the July Memorial Museum every year. Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, Liberation War Affairs Minister Ahmed Azam Khan, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed, Cultural Affairs Minister Nitai Roy Chowdhury and the Prime Minister's Adviser on Information and Cultural Affairs Dr Zahed Ur Rahman, among others, were present on the occasion. Earlier, the prime minister inaugurated the museum. Established at Ganabhaban, it has been created to preserve the authentic history of the July Mass Uprising, document the nation's resistance against autocracy, pass that legacy on to future generations and honour the sacrifices of the martyrs and the July fighters.

item.title: Govt websites restored after brief outage
item.description:
The Prime Minister's Office (PMO) website, pmo.gov.bd, and other Bangladesh government websites under the gov.bd domain became temporarily inaccessible on Tuesday morning before services were restored.
The disruption was first noticed around 10:15am. It affected websites of ministries, divisions, and government agencies, preventing users from accessing online services and information. The websites became accessible again around 11:45am.
During the disruption, visitors attempting to access the websites were shown the message: "Error 503 Backend fetch failed," along with "Guru Meditation" and a Varnish cache server notice.
While the disruption was ongoing, Prime Minister's Adviser on Posts, Telecommunications and Information Technology Rehan Asif Asad said authorities were aware of the issue and that a technical team was working to restore the services.
He later said: "The disruption was caused by a power-related issue, and the services are expected to be restored soon."
Abdullah Al Jaber, director of Cyber 71, said the error usually indicates server maintenance or a problem with network or server connectivity.
He said: "It cannot be directly described as a sign of a cyberattack."
However, he added that cyberattacks such as a distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attack can, in some cases, overload servers and trigger a 503 error.

item.title: NCP leader Tanvir sent to jail over Facebook post on PM
item.description:
A Bogra court on Wednesday sent Gazi Salahuddin Tanvir, the recently suspended joint member secretary of the National Citizen Party (NCP), to jail in a case filed over making a derogatory Facebook post about Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.
Judge Mehedi Hasan of Bogra Senior Judicial Magistrate Court passed the order.
Bogra Sadar police arrested him from the Monipur area of Dhaka on Tuesday night, said Sadar Police Station Officer-in-Charge Ibrahim Ali.
According to police and the case statement, Tanvir made the post following an alleged attack on an NCP street rally in Sylhet several days ago. The post triggered widespread reactions among BNP and its affiliated organisations’ leaders and activists.
Tanvir later deleted the post from Facebook and apologised. However, screenshots of the post circulated widely on social media and other platforms. The NCP subsequently suspended him from party activities and issued him a show-cause notice.
On August 2, Bogra Sadar upazila BNP President HS Maftun Ahmed Khan Rubel filed a case against Tanvir under the Cyber Security Act, 2026.
In the case statement, the complainant said he saw the Facebook post around 3pm on July 29 while at the Bogra district BNP office. He alleged that Tanvir had made defamatory and provocative comments targeting Prime Minister Tarique Rahman from his personal Facebook account.
The complainant said the post caused negative reactions among the public. Although it was later deleted, he alleged that the post amounted to an attempt to defame the prime minister and create confusion among the public. Several BNP leaders and activists had also seen the post on Facebook, the case statement added.
This marks the second time Tanvir has been suspended from the party. He was first removed in April 2025 following allegations that he interfered in deputy commissioner appointments after entering the secretariat in the aftermath of the July mass uprising and that he was involved in commission dealings related to textbook printing contracts with the National Curriculum and Textbook Board (NCTB).
He remained outside the party for about a year before being reinstated on April 16 this year. His latest suspension comes roughly three and a half months after his return.
Shortly after the controversy broke, Tanvir posted on his own Facebook account expressing regret over his remarks.

item.title: Children paint spirit of July at Parliament Secretariat competition
item.description:
The Parliament Secretariat on Wednesday organized a painting competition for children at the conference room of the North Plaza of the National Parliament, commemorating July Mass Uprising Day.
The theme of the competition was “July 24 Through the Brush," with children from schools in the capital taking part in two age groups: five to eight years and above eight to 12 years.
Shacot Ara Akter, MP, and Parliament Secretariat Secretary Barrister Md Golam Sorwar Bhuiyan visited the venue during the competition and interacted with the participants.
Speaking on the occasion, Shacot Ara said July symbolizes inspiration and collective consciousness, adding that the children’s paintings vividly reflected the spirit and memories associated with the July movement.
Golam Sorwar said the artworks demonstrated how children perceive and understand the significance of July, expressing hope that such initiatives will help future generations learn more about the events and their historical importance.
Senior officials of the Parliament Secretariat were also present at the program.

item.title: Fire breaks out at tobacco warehouse in Ashulia
item.description:
A fire broke out at a British American Tobacco (BAT) Bangladesh warehouse in Ashulia’s Nalam area on Wednesday morning.
The fire broke out around 7:30am, with seven Fire Service units working to bring it under control. Additional units have been kept on standby as the blaze spread rapidly through the warehouse.
Two units from Jirabo Fire Station initially responded, followed by two more from the same station, two from DEPZ Fire Station and one from Dhamrai Fire Station. Four Industrial Police teams are also assisting.
The fire has caused panic among nearby residents, some of whom moved their belongings to safer locations as a precaution.
Konok Chowdhury, senior station officer of DEPZ Fire Service, said it was too early to determine the cause of the fire or the extent of the damage.
“Six units are currently working to bring the fire under control. More units have been kept ready if needed. Details will be provided once the fire is brought under control,” he said.

Ishraque: Justice for July killings must be ensured
item.description:
State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain on Wednesday said the struggle will continue until those responsible for the murders during the July mass uprising are brought to justice.
He made the remarks while speaking after laying a wreath at the July Martyrs' Memorial at Shahbagh to pay tribute to those killed and injured during the July mass uprising.
“On behalf of my generation, I want to say that we have not forgotten July. We have not forgotten the July fighters. We will not stop until justice is ensured for the mass murders committed in Bangladesh,” Ishraque said.
Referring to recent developments, he said attempts were being made to create instability on campuses by forces that were on the side of the mass uprising.
The state minister alleged that the recent incidents could be part of a broader conspiracy.
“I think this could be part of a long-term conspiracy. Through this conspiracy, those from the fallen fascist regime, who looted thousands of crores of taka from Bangladesh, may try to reinvest that money to destabilise the country and eventually attempt to return,” he said.
Ishraque added that if deposed prime minister Sheikh Hasina attempted to return to Bangladesh, the death sentence awarded for the mass killings must be carried out. “That will mark the end of their role in Bangladesh's politics, InshaAllah,” he said.
Calling on all to remain vigilant, he said any attempt to destabilise the country or undermine a politically and democratically elected government through unrest will be resisted.

item.title: Bangladesh observes July Mass Uprising Day
item.description:
Bangladesh is observing July Mass Uprising Day today with nationwide programs, commemorating the student-led mass uprising that culminated in the fall of the Awami League government on August 5, 2024.
The day is being observed with state ceremonies, political programs and tributes to those killed and injured during the uprising.
The government, political parties and socio-cultural organisations have taken various programs, marking the day.
The minister, state minister, secretary, officials, and employees of the Ministry of Liberation War Affairs, along with people from different walks of life, placed wreaths at the July Martyrs' Memorial in Shahbagh on Wednesday morning.
At noon, a reception will be accorded to the families of the July martyrs and the July fighters at the Bangladesh-China Friendship Conference Centre in the capital. Acting President Hafiz Uddin Ahmad will attend the function as the chief guest.
Dhaka University is also observing the 2nd anniversary of the July Mass Uprising with a series of programs, including the foundation-laying of a July Memorial and a dedicated July Corner in the university's Central Library.
A discussion on the July uprising will be held at the TSC where five families of the July martyrs will be honoured, and a prayer session will be held after Asr prayers at the Central Mosque, seeking eternal peace for the martyrs.
Bangladesh missions abroad also chalked out discussion programs on the occasion.
Religious institutions across the country are organising special munajat and prayers.
Meanwhile, acting President Hafiz Uddin Ahmad and Prime Minister Tarique Rahman issued separate messages on the occasion of July Mass Uprising Day.
In his message, Hafiz Uddin Ahmad extended his heartfelt greetings and congratulations to the valiant July warriors and all patriotic citizens of the country, saying the nation will forever remember their extraordinary sacrifices, boundless courage and outstanding contributions as an enduring source of inspiration.
He also called for upholding the dignity of the martyrs’ sacrifices, building a humane Bangladesh that belongs to the people, where fascist and authoritarian rule, as well as extremism, will never again find a place.
The acting president urged all to unite in building a new Bangladesh that is democratic, just, humane, free from discrimination, happy and prosperous and work together to realise the dreams, ideals, hopes and aspirations of the martyrs who made the supreme sacrifice in the Great War of Independence and the July Mass Uprising.
In his message, the prime minister described August 5 as a day of joy, a day of victory and a day of the restoration of democratic political rights for all those who cherish freedom and democracy.
He said for more than one and a half decades, in the struggle against fascism and for the restoration of the people's right to vote and their democratic rights, the BNP, other anti-fascist political parties, and the people of differing views had to endure limitless persecution and repression.
Tarique Rahman said countless people became victims of enforced disappearance, murder, abduction, assaults, false cases, torture and oppression. “In leading this movement, the uncompromising leader of the nation, former Prime Minister late Begum Khaleda Zia, was also forced to spend years in the prison of the oppressors on false charges.”
He remembered with profound respect all the martyrs. “By sacrificing their lives for the freedom, rights and dignity of the country and its people, they have left us in their debt. Bangladesh owes an enduring debt to every martyr's family. Now it is our turn to repay that debt.”
The prime minister urged all to make a pledge to honour that debt through sincere efforts to build a just, self-reliant, democratic and humane Bangladesh by ensuring the political and economic empowerment of people and by establishing equality, human dignity and social justice.
Meanwhile, Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) has taken extensive and multi-layered security measures to maintain law and order and ensure public safety in the capital ahead of July Mass Uprising Day.
The measures have been taken to prevent any act of sabotage, untoward incident or disruption to public safety during the observance of the day, according to a DMP statement issued on Tuesday.
As part of the security plan, the number of police patrols and checkpoints has been significantly increased across the capital, with stricter search operations at all entry points to Dhaka.
On June 26, 2025, the government declared August 5 as July Mass Uprising Day. The day is a public holiday.

item.title: Teesta flows 13cm above danger level in Lalmonirhat
item.description:
The Teesta River was flowing 13 centimetres above the danger level at the Dalia point of the Teesta Barrage in Nilphamari on Wednesday morning as continuous rainfall and upstream hill runoff caused the water level to rise sharply.
Shunil Kumar, executive engineer of the Bangladesh Water Development Board (BWDB) in Lalmonirhat, said the water level was recorded at 9am.
As the river continued to swell, water began entering low-lying houses and agricultural land along its banks, he said.
However, no major financial losses are expected as there are currently no significant seasonal crops in the affected fields, the official said.
The BWDB said water levels in rivers across the northern region may continue to rise over the next 48 hours due to heavy rainfall and upstream inflows, potentially triggering minor flooding in low-lying areas.
All necessary preparations have been taken to respond to any flood-related situation, it said.

item.title: 52 tons of green chillis imported from India in two days
item.description:
Bangladesh imported nearly 52 tons of green chillies from India through the Benapole land port in two days amid a sharp rise in prices in the local markets.
On Tuesday evening, three Indian trucks carrying 42,220kg of green chillies entered the port. Another 9,200kg arrived on Monday, taking the two-day total to 51,420kg.
The consignments were cleared and sent to different parts of the country soon after completing port formalities. Shimu Enterprise imported the chillies, with Shimu Shipping Lines acting as the C&F agent.
Benapole Land Port Director (Traffic) Shamim Hossain said several more trucks carrying green chillies are waiting across the border and are expected to enter Bangladesh in the coming days.
Importer Rafiqul Islam said green chillies are being imported from India at $305 per ton. He expects increased imports to bring down prices, which have already fallen to Tk240-250 per kg at the Benapole market from Tk300 on Monday.
The government recently allowed green chilli imports from India to address rising prices and supply shortages. In the first phase, 69 traders received permits to import 29,710 tons of green chillies.

item.title: Swapon: Feb-12 election least controversial in Bangladesh's history
item.description:
Information and Broadcasting Minister Zahir Uddin Swapon on Tuesday said the February-12 election was the least controversial among all parliamentary polls held in Bangladesh.
"In Bangladesh, 13 parliamentary elections were held. The most recent election was the least controversial of them all," he said while addressing a discussion, marking the 2nd anniversary of July Mass Uprising at the Council Building of the Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (Buet) here.
The minister said Bangladesh has not attained the desired institutional framework for the executive, judiciary and legislature yet.
“But we cannot say we have reached the place of our desired judicial system. Even in the light of the thought based on common democratic values, we have not yet achieved the institutional structures required for the executive branch, the judiciary, the legislative branch of the state,” he said, claiming that Bangladesh has never passed through a stable socio-economic system.
Referring to the 2024 July Mass Uprising, Swapon expressed optimism that the aspirations created following the sacrifices made by the martyrs of the July Uprising will enter a final stage, so that the country's socio-economic system will never again have to fall into this constraint.
He said if the country truly wants to achieve such a desired state, it must first understand why these repeated instabilities occurred and whether the root causes have been removed.
“If we try to look at July Mass Uprising from a research perspective, then we will truly be paying our respects to the martyrs of July Uprising,” he said.
Buet Teachers' Association President Prof Muhammad Anisuzzaman Talukder chaired the discussion, while Buet Pro-Vice Chancellor Prof Mohammad Shariful Islam attended it as a special guest.
Former Buet pro-VC Prof Abdul Hasib Chowdhury and Dean of the Faculty of Civil Engineering Prof Md Abdul Jalil were present as guests of honour in the event.

item.title: Renowned folk singer Mujib Pardeshi lands in jail
item.description:
A Dhaka court on Tuesday sent renowned folk singer, composer and music director Mujib Pardeshi to jail in a Tk10 lakh cheque dishonour case.
Dhaka Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Md Sefatullah passed the order after police produced the accused before the court. Idris Ali Biswas filed the case with Magura court in 2022.
On March 15, 2023, the 2nd Joint District and Sessions Judge of Magura Muhammad Anwar Sadat sentenced Pardeshi to one year's rigorous imprisonment and fined him Tk10 lakh, the value of the dishonoured cheque. As he remained absconding, the court subsequently issued an arrest warrant against him. Police from Uttara West Police Station arrested Pardeshi on Monday.
SI Helal Uddin of the prosecution division said police sought an order to keep the accused in custody after producing him before the court. The court ordered that he be sent to jail.
No lawyer appeared on behalf of Pardeshi during the hearing. However, the complainant's counsel Shafiqul Islam opposed bail, arguing that the accused had remained absconding despite being aware of the case and had shown disregard for the legal process. He urged the court to reject the bail petition, saying Pardeshi's release could prejudice the complainant's interests.
Mujib Pardeshi, whose real name is Mujibur Rahman Molla, is a renowned Bangladeshi folk singer, composer and music director. He rose to prominence in the 1980s with his Bengali folk and traditional songs.

item.title: People in Gazipur plant paddy seedlings on unfinished road
item.description:
Residents of Sreepur upazila in Gazipur planted paddy saplings on an unfinished road protesting the prolonged suspension of a development project after the contractor allegedly abandoned the work nearly two years ago.
The protest was held on Monday on a two-kilometre stretch of the Nayanpur-Barmi road, where construction work has remained incomplete, causing severe suffering for thousands of commuters.
The six-kilometre road connects residents of Gafargaon and South Gafargaon upazilas of Mymensingh with Sreepur’s Kawraid, Barmi and Telihati unions. Locals said the damaged road has disrupted the movement of industrial workers, students and residents in the area.
The Local Government Engineering Department (LGED) awarded the road improvement contract to Messrs Shammi Enterprise under the 2024-25 GOB Maintenance Project-3. The project, funded by the government’s revenue budget, was estimated to cost Tk4.09 crore.
The work, which started in mid-2024, involved repairing the road from Nayanpur Bazar to CCDB Mor. However, after digging up the road and laying brick chips, the contractor stopped work and has remained absent from the site, according to locals.
A visit to the area found that the road has developed numerous potholes as the brick chips were washed away over time. Rainwater has accumulated in several places, making the road hazardous for vehicles and pedestrians.
Local traders Rakib Mia, Sultan Uddin and Mostafa Kamal said the road becomes almost unusable after rainfall.
“After rain, it becomes difficult to tell where the road ends and the potholes begin. People fall, vehicles get stuck, and businesses are suffering,” they said.
Auto-rickshaw driver Sumon Mia said he has been unable to operate on the road for nearly two years, resulting in a significant drop in his income.
“A few weeks ago, some workers were seen at the site, but now all work has stopped. No one from the contractor’s side can be found in the area,” he said.
Local physician Shamsul Islam Tarek said residents had welcomed the repair initiative when it began but are now facing greater difficulties.
“Before the repair work started, we could still use the road. Now travelling has become extremely difficult. We urge the administration to take immediate steps to complete the work,” he said.
Attempts to contact Ziaur Rahman, owner of Messrs Shammi Enterprise, were unsuccessful as he did not respond to repeated phone calls.
Sreepur Upazila Engineer Touhid Hasan said the authorities had repeatedly notified the contractor to resume work but failed to get a response.
“Considering public suffering, we have informed higher authorities about imposing penalties and cancelling the work order. A fresh tender process will be initiated soon,” he said.
He blamed the contractor’s negligence for the delay and said the project would be completed after cancelling the existing contract and appointing a new contractor through a fresh tender.

Measles: Death toll stands at 849 as two children die in 24 hours
item.description:
Bangladesh's combined death toll from confirmed and suspected measles cases has risen to 849 after two more children died from measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours until 8:00am on Tuesday, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
The DGHS classified both of the latest fatalities as suspected measles deaths. With the latest update, the number of suspected measles-related deaths has climbed to 753, while laboratory-confirmed measles deaths remained unchanged at 96.
The country also recorded 896 new suspected measles cases during the reporting period, raising the cumulative number of suspected infections to 131,946.
Meanwhile, health authorities confirmed 123 new measles infections through laboratory testing, bringing the total number of confirmed cases nationwide to 16,531.
DGHS data also showed that since March 15, a total of 114,393 patients with suspected measles have been hospitalized across the country. Of them, 110,187 have recovered.

item.title: Chhatra Dal, Shibir activists clash at Dhaka College
item.description:
A clash broke out between activists of Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal (JCD) and Bangladesh Islami Chhatra Shibir at Dhaka College on Tuesday afternoon, triggering panic and heightening tensions on the campus.
The violence erupted around 4:30pm, with the rival groups engaging in several rounds of chases and counter-chases.
An officer on duty at New Market Police Station said senior police officials, along with additional police personnel, rushed to the scene after receiving reports of the clash.
Witnesses said Chhatra Dal activists later gathered at the Science Laboratory intersection carrying sticks, as tensions remained high in and around the campus.
The rival student organizations traded blame over the incident. Chhatra Dal alleged its activists were attacked while heading to a workers' meeting, while Chhatra Shibir claimed Chhatra Dal activists launched the attack as it was preparing to hold a reception and discussion program for the families of those killed in the July mass uprising. Neither claim could be independently verified.
Chhatra Dal claimed 11 of its activists were injured in the clash, while Chhatra Shibir claimed more than 20 of its members were hurt, taking the total number of injured to more than 30, according to the two organizations. The injury claims could not be independently verified.
Earlier in the day, similar clashes broke out between Chhatra Dal and Chhatra Shibir activists at Jagannath University and Government Madrasah-e-Alia.
The campuses remained under heightened tension in the aftermath of the clashes.

Two rounds of Chhatra Dal-Shibir clashes hit JnU: Both claim scores injured
item.description:
At least two rounds of clashes broke out between activists of Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal (JCD) and Bangladesh Islami Chhatra Shibir at Jagannath University (JnU) on Tuesday, with both groups claiming that more than 50 of their activists and students were injured.
The first clash erupted on the university campus around noon, while the second broke out later outside Dhaka National Medical Institute Hospital, where police intervened to restore order.
Witnesses said the initial clash occurred during a programme marking the July Mass Uprising Day at the university's central auditorium, attended by University Grants Commission (UGC) Chairman Prof Dr Mamun Ahmed as the chief guest.
According to witnesses, Shibir activists entered the venue carrying placards highlighting various student demands, prompting a heated exchange with Chhatra Dal activists that quickly escalated into a clash.
Following the violence, Chhatra Dal activists forced Shibir members off the campus and staged a protest rally.
Around 2:00pm, activists from different units of Chhatra Shibir gathered at Dhaka National Medical Institute Hospital to visit those injured in the earlier clash. At the same time, Chhatra Dal activists assembled outside the hospital's main gate, chanting slogans.
The rival groups again engaged in chases and counter-chases, forcing Shibir activists to take shelter inside the hospital. Witnesses said both sides hurled brickbats at each other, while several individuals were seen carrying locally made weapons.
Jagannath University Central Students' Union (JnUCSU) Vice-President Md Riazul Islam, who is backed by Chhatra Shibir, alleged that Shibir activists had attended the programme with placards to draw the UGC chairman's attention to student demands.
"However, the university administration, several teachers and Chhatra Dal activists prevented us from doing so. At one stage, Chhatra Dal activists attacked us, snatched our placards and assaulted our members, leaving around 50 students injured," he claimed.
Denying the allegation, Chhatra Dal Member Secretary Shamsul Arefin accused Shibir of attempting to divert attention from the alleged failures of the JnUCSU leadership and the activities of Jamaat-Shibir.
"They tried to create mob violence at Jagannath University, similar to what happened at Begum Rokeya University. Since August 5, they have repeatedly promoted mob culture," he alleged.
Jagannath University Vice-Chancellor Professor Dr Md Rais Uddin said a programme marking the July Mass Uprising Day was underway at the auditorium when "a group attempted to create disorder outside."
"We suspect that forces opposed to the July movement may have been involved. We will also investigate whether the Chhatra League had any role in the incident," he said.
As of filing this report, Chhatra Dal activists were continuing demonstrations and chanting slogans on the university campus and outside Dhaka National Medical Institute Hospital, while Chhatra Shibir activists remained inside the hospital.

item.title: Call for integrated action on climate and early childhood development
item.description:
Policymakers, development experts, and civil society representatives on Tuesday called for coordinated action to address the climate crisis while ensuring children's early development, saying the two priorities are closely interconnected and essential to building a sustainable future.
They urged the government, development partners, civil society, the media, the private sector, and families to work together to safeguard children's wellbeing while protecting the environment.
The call came at a policy dialogue titled What to Do for Childhood: Protecting Childhood and the Earth , jointly organized by the Bangladesh Early Childhood Development Network (BEN) and the Prokriti O Jibon Foundation, with support from Arnec and Somasti Media Communication and Development Foundation. Channel i served as the event's media partner.
Addressing the event as chief guest, Women and Children Affairs Minister Dr AZM Zahid Hossain said investment in early childhood development is one of the country's most important long-term investments rather than an expense.
He said raising public awareness, ensuring adequate financial investment, strengthening policy implementation, and enhancing institutional support are essential to addressing climate change and creating a safe, child-friendly environment. He also stressed the need for close collaboration among the government, development partners, private organizations, the media, and civil society.
Presiding over the event, Prokriti O Jibon Foundation Chairman Mukit Majumder Babu said protecting children's care, development, and wellbeing must go hand in hand with conserving nature, the environment, and biodiversity to leave a livable planet for future generations.
He said investing in children today and protecting the Earth are equally important for building a stronger and more humane society.
Presenting the keynote paper, BEN Vice-President Mahmuda Akter highlighted the importance of the first 1,000 days of a child's life, describing it as the most critical period for physical, cognitive, social, and emotional development.
She said ensuring proper nutrition, healthcare, responsive caregiving, a nurturing family environment, and early learning opportunities during this period significantly improves a child's lifelong potential, calling for increased public and private investment.
The discussion featured representatives from UNICEF Bangladesh, UNESCO, government agencies, universities, and development organizations, including Save the Children Bangladesh, Plan International Bangladesh, Synergos, Manusher Jonno Foundation, BRAC University, Independent University, Bangladesh, North South University, and the Department of Social Services.
Speakers said many families in Bangladesh remain unaware of the importance of early childhood development, resulting in gaps in nutrition, healthcare, quality caregiving, safe environments, and pre-primary education. They stressed the need to raise public awareness, strengthen parental capacity, expand community-level services, and improve community engagement.
They also emphasized that children are among the most vulnerable to the impacts of climate change and called for greater investment in child-centered climate adaptation and sustainable development planning.
The speakers agreed that ensuring children's wellbeing and protecting the environment require stronger coordination among government institutions, development partners, educational institutions, the private sector, the media, and civil society. They urged policymakers to place children's rights, safety, and environmental conservation at the center of national development planning.

item.title: Shibir-JCD clash leaves Dhaka Alia Madrasa principal among 10 injured
item.description:
The principal of Dhaka Alia Madrasa and nine others were injured after activists of Islami Chhatra Shibir and Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal (JCD) clashed on Tuesday afternoon over a dispute involving dormitory seats.
The violence erupted outside the campus, where activists from both groups exchanged brickbats and engaged in several rounds of chases and counter-chases, according to witnesses and campus sources.
Among the injured was the madrasa's principal Mahmud Obaidul Haque, 52, who was rescued by teachers and students and taken to the emergency department of Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH) at around 5:00pm. He is currently undergoing treatment in Ward No 4.
Also injured were Shamim Mahmud, 30, president of JCD's Dhaka South unit; Sanaullah, 30, former senior joint convener of the Government Alia Madrasa unit of JCD; and Nesar Uddin Rabbi, 27, member secretary of Lalbagh Thana JCD. They were later taken to DMCH for treatment.
Sabbir Rahman, who accompanied the injured to the hospital, confirmed their identities.
Inspector Md Faruk, in-charge of the DMCH Police camp, confirmed that the injured are receiving treatment at the hospital. Police rushed to the scene and brought the situation under control, though tension continued to prevail in the area.
Shibir alleged that its activists were attacked after protesting what it described as the illegal occupation of dormitory seats.
JCD, however, claimed that Shibir was deliberately trying to destabilise educational institutions through planned violence.
As of 6:00pm, when this report was filed, the clashes had subsided, but the campus remained tense. Additional police personnel were deployed, and law enforcement agencies continued to monitor the situation.
Chawkbazar Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Md Mamun said the clash occurred outside the campus between activists of JCD and Shibir, leaving several members of both groups injured.
"The situation is now under control, and police have been deployed in the area," he said.
Meanwhile, separate clashes between activists of Islami Chhatra Shibir and JCD also broke out at Jagannath University and Dhaka College on Tuesday, raising fresh concerns over security at educational institutions across the capital.
Dhaka Metropolitan Police Additional Commissioner Osman Gani told DhakaTribune that clashes had occurred at all three campuses. "Police intervened and brought the situations under control. The situation is now normal, and additional personnel have been deployed on the campuses," he said.

item.title: Faridpur DB OC, 10 others face departmental action over Chhatra League man's custodial death
item.description:
An internal investigation by Faridpur district police has recommended departmental proceedings against the then officer-in-charge (OC) of the Detective Branch (DB) and 10 other police personnel over the custodial death of banned Bangladesh Chhatra League (BCL) activist Mirza Ishtiaq Ahmed Pranto.
The report of the probe has already been sent to Police Headquarters for further action, Faridpur Superintendent of Police Shahriar Muhammad Miajee said on Tuesday.
"The internal investigation recommended initiating departmental proceedings against the 11 DB members, including the OC, and taking disciplinary action against them," he told reporters.
Pranto, a resident of West Gondhardia in Madhukhali upazila, was picked up by DB police from in front of his house by the Dhaka-Khulna highway on June 20.
According to police, he fell ill while in DB custody and died at Faridpur Medical College Hospital the following day.
A student of Faridpur Law College, Pranto also worked as a seasonal labourer at Faridpur Sugar Mills.
On June 21, Sub-Inspector Ahaduzzaman, who took part in the operation, filed a narcotics case at Madhukhali Police Station, claiming that 100 grams of cannabis were recovered from Pranto.
According to the case statement, the raid took place around 2am on June 21. During the raid, Pranto admitted possessing the drugs before handing them over from a pocket of his trousers in the presence of two witnesses.
However, a video of the incident that later surfaced appeared to show the operation taking place during daylight, with Pranto wearing a lungi instead of trousers.
The two witnesses named in the case also told investigators that they were not present at the scene during the recovery and signed documents later after being misled and intimidated.
Pranto's mother Khadija Akter alleged that DB personnel demanded Tk65,000 for her son's release on the night of his detention and later asked her to bring Tk100,000 the following morning.
She said she arrived with the money but received her son's body instead.
As the news drew huge flak, the district police formed a three-member internal investigation committee headed by Additional Superintendent of Police (Administration and Finance) Fatema Islam.
The committee also included Additional Superintendent of Police (Crime and Operations) Md Shamsul Azam and district Special Branch OC Mosharraf Hossain.
SP Miajee said the probe found that all officers involved in the operation had some level of responsibility and recommended a departmental investigation to determine each individual's role before further action is taken.
He, however, declined to comment on specific inconsistencies surrounding the case, including the drug recovery, discrepancies over the timing of the operation, the presence of the witnesses and allegations that money was demanded from the victim's family.
Following the incident, the then DB OC and the 10 other police personnel involved in the operation were attached to the Faridpur Police Lines.

item.title: Two madrasa teachers sent to jail in student murder case
item.description:
A Dhaka court on Tuesday sent two madrasa teachers to jail in a murder case filed over the death of a 13-year-old student whose body was recovered from a washroom at a madrasa in the capital's Kadamtali area.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Hasibuzzaman passed the order after the investigation officer produced the accused before the court and sought their detention pending investigation.
SI Abdus Sabur of the Dhaka Metropolitan Court's Prosecution Division confirmed the matter.
The accused are Hafez Md Zakaria, 35, and Hafez Md Zobayer Ahmed, 20, teachers at Rowajatul Ulum Hafezia Nurani Madrasa in the Jorakhamba area of Rayerbagh.
According to court sources, the investigation officer and Sub-Inspector Amzad Hossain of Kadamtali Police Station produced the two accused before the court and sought an order to keep them in jail. No lawyer appeared on behalf of the accused during the hearing.
The body of 13-year-old Md Naeem Sheikh was recovered from a third-floor washroom of the madrasa on Monday afternoon.
Later that day, the victim's mother Nazma Begum filed a murder case with Kadamtali Police Station against the two teachers. Police arrested them from the madrasa the same night.
According to the first information report (FIR), Nazma's two sons studied at the madrasa, where Naeem was allegedly subjected to repeated physical abuse by the accused teachers.
The FIR states that after learning about the alleged abuse, Nazma sought to withdraw her son from the madrasa, but the teachers refused to issue him a transfer certificate.
It further alleges that at around 1:00pm on Monday, Naeem told the teachers he no longer wanted to study at the madrasa. He was allegedly beaten and forcibly confined before being strangled to death between 1:00pm and 2:30pm, according to the complaint.

item.title: Yemen’s Houthis say attacked southern Saudi airport
item.description:
Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis said on Tuesday that they had attacked an airport in Saudi Arabia, as tensions between the two foes brewed after the rebels declared a maritime blockade on Riyadh and struck its ships.
Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said they “successfully targeted a sensitive target belonging to the Saudi enemy at Najran Airport using a drone,” adding that the strike on the southern airport was “in response to the Saudi enemy’s violation of airspace over the Saada and Hajjah governorates using drones.”
A regional source with knowledge of the matter told AFP that the airport’s main radar was hit, affecting operations.
Saudi Arabia has not, so far, issued any comment on the claimed attack.

item.title: Court orders fresh CID probe into Primeasia Student Parvez murder
item.description:
A Dhaka court on Tuesday ordered the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) to carry out a further investigation into the murder of Primeasia University student and Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal leader Zahidul Islam Parvez.
Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Md Sefatullah passed the order after hearing a protest petition (naraji) filed by the complainant against the police charge sheet.
The court directed the CID to submit its investigation report by September 7, state prosecutor Harun-or-Rashid said.
Parvez, a Textile Engineering student at the Banani-based private university, was fatally stabbed during a clash between students of the Textile Engineering and English departments shortly after 4:00pm on April 19 last year.
The following day, the victim's cousin, Humayun Kabir, filed a murder case with Banani Police Station.
After completing the investigation, Banani Police Inspector AKM Moin Uddin submitted a charge sheet to the court on April 29, accusing nine people, including two women.
The charge-sheeted accused are Meheraj Islam, Abu Johor Giffari alias Piyas, Md Mahathir Hasan, Md Al Kamal Sheikh alias Kamal, Alvi Hossain Junayed, Al Amin Sani, Fatema Tahsin Oishi, Faria Haque Tina and Rakib.
The investigating officer, however, recommended the discharge of eight other accused, including Sobhan Niaz Tushar, joint convener of the Anti-Discrimination Student Movement in Banani, citing insufficient evidence.
The others recommended for discharge are Maruf Miaji Hridoy, Rifat, Ali, Fahim, Sakib, Nasim and Nibir.
Humayun Kabir challenged the recommendation by filing a protest petition, alleging that the investigation was incomplete and flawed.
Advocate Mohammad Afzal Hossain Mridha represented the complainant during Tuesday's hearing, while Harun-or-Rashid appeared for the prosecution.
After hearing both sides, the court ordered the CID to conduct a further investigation into the case.

item.title: Two killed in separate road accidents in Dhaka
item.description:
Two people were killed and two others injured in separate road accidents in the capital early Tuesday.
Badda Police Station Sub-Inspector (SI) Md Mahbub Alam said three friends were riding a motorcycle towards the Middle Badda U-loop Bridge at around 2:30am when another motorcycle coming from the opposite direction collided with them and fled the scene.
All three riders were rescued and taken to hospital. One of them, Hasan, who sustained critical injuries, was taken to Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH), where doctors declared him dead at around 3:30am.
The two other injured riders were admitted to the National Institute of Traumatology and Orthopaedic Rehabilitation (NITOR), commonly known as Pangu Hospital.
Hasan was the son of Md Munna of Mirjanagar Alabari village in Begumganj upazila of Noakhali. He worked as a ride-sharing driver and lived in the South Banasree area of Dhaka.
In a separate incident, an unidentified woman was killed after being hit by a bus in the Staff Quarter area of Demra at around 4am.
Demra Police Station SI Mahbur Rahman said police rescued the woman from the roadside and took her to DMCH, where she was declared dead at around 5:30am.
Police said the woman, believed to be around 30 years old, appeared to be a vagrant who often stayed in the area. Her identity has not yet been established.
The body has been sent to the DMCH morgue for an autopsy.

item.title: Adviser Zahed: Media defying court order on Hasina speeches to face action
item.description:
The government will take necessary action against any media outlet that publishes or broadcasts speeches by former prime minister Sheikh Hasina in violation of a court order, Prime Minister's Information and Broadcasting Adviser Dr Zahed Ur Rahman said on Tuesday.
"The government earlier issued an advisory for the media in this regard. If any media outlet announces in advance that Sheikh Hasina will deliver a speech and then publishes or broadcasts it, it will amount to defying the court order," he said at a press briefing held at the Secretariat.
He said the government would once again remind all media outlets to refrain from such activities, stressing that complying with court directives is the responsibility of every individual and institution.
"The government's responsibility is to ensure implementation of the court's decisions," he added.
Expressing his personal opinion, the adviser said he would not have supported restricting the broadcast of Hasina's speeches had there been no court order.
"If anyone disagrees with the court's order, they have the right to challenge it before the court. But as long as the order remains in force, everyone must comply with it," he said.
Replying to a question on why the government came to know about former IGP Benazir Ahmed's bail two to three days after it was granted, Zahed said he was not confirmed about the matter and could not provide an immediate explanation.
Responding to another question on whether the previous government's influence still exists in the administration and other institutions, the adviser said the fall of Sheikh Hasina's government and her departure from the country on August 5 marked a significant event in Bangladesh's history. However, he said it is not possible to replace all officials who served at different levels of the administration during the previous 15 years overnight.
"Many people associated with the previous government are still working in different institutions, including the administration. It is simply not possible to remove such a large number of people at once; the process takes time," he said.

item.title: PM meets experts, assures cooperation for safe water management
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Monday assured experts and representatives of relevant organisations of the government’s cooperation in ensuring safe and sustainable water management as part of its commitment to environmental protection and sustainable development.
He made the assurance while exchanging views with experts and representatives of organisations working in the water, environment and engineering sectors on the country’s water management challenges and possible long-term solutions.
The meeting was held in the Prime Minister’s Office at Bangladesh Secretariat, said PM’s Deputy Press Secretary Hasan Shiplu.
He said the discussion focused on restoring canals, ensuring the stability of rivers and embankments, improving urban drainage systems, wastewater treatment and rainwater management.
The experts and representatives also stressed the need for integrated and effective urban planning to address the challenges posed by rapid urbanisation.
Led by Footsteps Bangladesh, experts from the environment, water and engineering sectors, along with representatives of several organisations working in the field, attended the meeting.
They shared their experiences and recommendations on the country’s water management challenges, existing limitations and possible solutions.
The experts recommended adopting short, medium and long term plans, expanding the use of modern technologies, strengthening coordination among relevant agencies and taking effective measures in view of the impacts of climate change.
After hearing the experts' views and recommendations, the Prime Minister assured them of the government's support to ensure safe and effective water management for citizens in line with its commitment to sustainable development and environmental protection, said Hasan Shiplu.
State Minister for LGRD and Cooperatives Mir Shahe Alam, Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister ABM Abdus Sattar and BNP Special Secretary Belayet Hossain, among others, were present.
The experts and representatives include Footsteps Bangladesh Trustee and Head of Partnerships Fasbeer Eskander, President Shah Rafayat Chowdhury, Vice-President Mohammad Taqi Yasir, former Chief Engineer of the World Bank’s Waste Management Project Tariq Bin Yousuf , Professor Mujibur Rahman of United International University, Red Orange Director Alok Kumar Majumdar, Deputy Director Samiul Islam, Youth for NDC Executive Director Amanullah Parag, GarbageMan founder and CEO Fahim Uddin Shuvo and urban and rural planner SM Mehedi Hasan.

Osaka out to improve Toronto fortunes with eye on US Open
item.description:
Naomi Osaka is hoping her success last year in Montreal, where she finished runner-up to Victoria Mboko, will translate as the WTA's 1000 event in Canada shifts to Toronto.
The four-time Grand Slam champion from Japan is coming off a semi-final run on the hard courts of Washington, where she fell to eventual champion Alexandra Eala of the Philippines.
"I did better than last year in DC, so I'm just hoping to keep the ball rolling," Osaka said.
"I haven't historically played super, super well here, so I'm just hoping to change that this year.
"I can try to recall Montreal, but I would like to kind of treat the cities separately," added Osaka, whose best run in Toronto -- which alternates hosting duties with Montreal each year -- was a quarter-final appearance back in 2019.
The former world number one is seeded 11th this year and aiming to build momentum as the August 31 start of the US Open approaches.
Osaka earned the last of her four major titles at the 2021 Australian Open and has yet to regain the heights she reached before taking an extended maternity leave in 2023.
But she made it to the US Open semi-finals last year and reached the last 16 at the French Open for the first time this year before a career-best quarter-final at Wimbledon.
"I would just hope to gain a lot of confidence leading into New York," she said.
"I lost my last match, but it's helped me figure out what I want to do exactly, or how I want to take my tennis."
Osaka is in the same quarter as second-seeded Australian Open champion Elena Rybakina and in the fourth round she could find herself up against fifth-seeded French Open champion Mirra Andreeva.
Andreeva, who suffered a shock second-round exit at Wimbledon, will face a tricky opening match against former world number one Karolina Pliskova, who beat Ukraine's Oleksandra Oliynykova 6-4, 6-4 on Monday.
Osaka will open against Hungary's Panna Uvardy, who was up 2-6, 7-6 (7/3), 2-0 against Eva Lys when the German retired because of injury in a match in which she led the second set 5-2.
It was a jam-packed schedule on the second day of first-round play.
Among the winners, Poland's Magdalena Frech defeated France's Leolia Jeanjean 7-5, 6-3 to line up a meeting with third-seeded two-time champion Jessica Pegula.
Pegula beat Frech last week on the way to the final in Washington, where the American fell to Eala in the rain-delayed title match on Monday.
In other early matches, American Kayla Day beat Diane Parry of France 3-6, 6-3, 7-5 to book a clash with fourth-seeded Coco Gauff.
World number one Aryna Sabalenka is the top seed in the tournament.
After disappointing runs at the French Open and Wimbledon the Belarusian is aiming to reassert her dominance on hard courts, where her lone defeat this year was to Rybakina in the Australian Open final.

item.title: Dhaka air quality moderate Tuesday morning
item.description:
Dhaka ranked 30th among the world's most polluted cities on Tuesday morning, recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 73 at 8:55 am.
According to the AQI scale, the city's air quality was classified as ‘Moderate ', posing a moderate health concern for a very small number of unusually sensitive individuals (such as people with asthma, heart disease, or older adults).
Riyadh of Saudi Arabia topped the global pollution list with an AQI score of 183, followed by Doha of the Qatar with 161 Kuwait City of Kuwait with 160.
According to AQI standards, a reading between 101 and 150 is considered ‘unhealthy for sensitive groups’, 151 to 200 ‘unhealthy’, 201 to 300 ‘very unhealthy’, while levels above 301 are deemed ‘hazardous’, posing serious health risks.
The AQI, which provides daily updates on air quality, indicates how clean or polluted the air is and highlights potential health impacts.
In Bangladesh, the AQI is calculated based on five major pollutants: particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), sulfur dioxide (SO2), and ozone.
Dhaka has long struggled with air pollution, with air quality typically worsening in winter and improving during the monsoon season.
The World Health Organization estimates that air pollution causes around seven million deaths globally each year, mainly due to stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer and acute respiratory infections.
