Dinesh Trivedi: Dhaka, Delhi have potential to become global economic powerhouse
item.description:
Indian High Commissioner to Bangladesh Dinesh Trivedi on Monday said Bangladesh and India possess all the ingredients necessary to emerge as a global economic powerhouse. During a meeting with the leaders of International Chamber of Commerce-Bangladesh (ICC Bangladesh) at its Secretariat, he observed that both countries have exceptional strengths in innovation, education, healthcare and human capital, and stressed that these advantages should be translated into stronger economic cooperation and sustainable development.
The High Commissioner said many longstanding bilateral issues could be resolved through sustained engagement and dialogue at the highest political level.
He emphasised the indispensable role of the private sector in driving economic growth, investment and employment, noting that businesses are the foundation of a stable and prosperous economy.
The Indian envoy also highlighted the significant opportunities for establishing joint venture industries in border areas, which could strengthen regional value chain, attract investment and create employment.
Reaffirming the High Commission's commitment to supporting the business community, he encouraged Bangladeshi entrepreneurs and investors to approach the High Commission whenever they encounter challenges in expanding bilateral trade and investment. At the meeting, both sides exchanged views on strengthening bilateral trade, investment and regional economic cooperation.
Welcoming the High Commissioner, ICC Bangladesh President Mahbubur Rahman highlighted the longstanding friendship and growing economic partnership between Bangladesh and India.
He underscored the importance of stronger private sector engagement to unlock the full potential of bilateral cooperation and promote sustainable economic growth.
Bangladesh and India continue to enjoy largest trading relationships in South Asia. Bilateral merchandise trade reached approximately US$11.39 billion in FY2024–25, with Bangladesh exporting goods worth US$1.76 billion to India and importing US$9.62 billion.
The ICC Bangladesh President emphasised the importance of improving market access for Bangladeshi products, reducing non-tariff barriers, harmonising standards, simplifying customs procedures and concluding the proposed Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) at the earliest opportunity to reduce the trade gap. The meeting also discussed opportunities to deepen cooperation in investment, regional value chain, multimodal connectivity, renewable energy, cross-border power trade, digital commerce, fintech, artificial intelligence, climate finance, sustainable manufacturing, healthcare, education and skills development.
ICC Bangladesh President further highlighted the importance of revitalising regional cooperation through SAARC, expediting implementation of the Bangladesh-Bhutan-India-Nepal (BBIN) Motor Vehicles Agreement, and advancing practical cooperation under BIMSTEC to enhance connectivity, reduce logistics costs and strengthen regional supply chains.
Rahman reiterated the importance of resolving the anti-dumping measures affecting Bangladeshi exports, particularly jute and jute products, and called for continued dialogue to ensure fair and transparent trade remedies.
During the interactive discussion, ICC Bangladesh Vice-President Naser Ejaz Bijoy emphasised the importance of facilitating business travel and called for further improvement in the issuance of business visas to strengthen commercial engagement between the two countries.
ICC Bangladesh Executive Board Member Simeen Rahman highlighted the vast opportunities for expanding bilateral cooperation in trade, business, healthcare, medical services and tourism.
She noted that India is home to many globally recognised companies and institutions, creating significant potential for enhanced partnerships and greater people-to-people and business-to-business collaboration.
ICC Bangladesh Executive Board Member Abdul Hai Sarker expressed his optimism that many of the longstanding unresolved bilateral trade and business issues could be addressed during the tenure of the new High Commissioner, paving the way for stronger economic cooperation between the two neighbouring countries.
Speaking on behalf of the business community, ICC Bangladesh reaffirmed its commitment to promoting stronger business-to-business cooperation through joint business councils, CEO forums, SME collaboration, startup exchanges, investment missions and technology partnerships.
The ICC Bangladesh President expressed its commitment to working closely with the High Commission of India and ICC India, under the aegis of the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI), to further strengthen economic collaboration and promote a more prosperous, sustainable and mutually beneficial future for both Bangladesh and India.
The Meeting was also attended by ICCB Executive Board Member Tapan, Chowdhury, Pawan Kumar Badhe, Deputy High Commissioner of India to Bangladesh, Gourab Kumar Agarwal, Second Secretary (Economic & Commerce) High Commission of India to Bangladesh, ICCB Secretary General Ataur Rahman, General Manager Ajay Bihari Saha & Deputy General Manager Syeda Shahnewaz Lotika.

item.title: PM seeks greater South Korean investment ahead of CEPA
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Monday urged South Korean companies to expand investment in Bangladesh, highlighting opportunities in shipbuilding, semiconductors, electronics, telecommunications, automotive manufacturing and the toy industry, as both countries move closer to signing a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA).
The PM made the call when South Korean Trade Minister Yeo Han-koo made a courtesy call on him at the Cabinet Division of the Bangladesh Secretariat on Monday, sai the Prime Minister's Deputy Press Secretary Shahadat Shadhin.
At the meeting, Yeo briefed the prime minister on the progress of the CEPA, saying the agreement is awaiting signing and is expected to significantly boost bilateral trade, economic cooperation and South Korean investment in Bangladesh once it comes into effect.
He said many South Korean companies are already operating successfully in Bangladesh and that many more are interested in investing in the country.
Rahman invited South Korean investors to explore opportunities in Bangladesh's toy manufacturing, electronics, telecommunications, automotive, semiconductor and shipbuilding sectors.
Noting South Korea's global expertise in shipbuilding and Bangladesh's large workforce, the prime minister proposed establishing training centers in Bangladesh to provide technical and language training for workers, enabling them to contribute to South Korea's shipbuilding industry.
He also assured South Korean companies of the government's full support for investments in Bangladesh's shipbuilding sector.
The two sides also discussed organizing a seminar involving South Korean companies operating in Bangladesh.
Yeo was briefed on various government initiatives to further improve the country's investment climate.
In response, the South Korean minister said Bangladesh's proposals would help strengthen bilateral relations in the years ahead.
Rahman also invited the South Korean president to pay an official visit to Bangladesh.
Commerce, Industries, Textiles and Jute Minister Khandaker Abdul Muktadir, Prime Minister's Adviser on Economic Affairs and Planning Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir, Foreign Affairs Adviser Humayun Kabir, Bangladesh Investment Development Authority (BIDA) Executive Chairman Ashik Chowdhury and other senior officials attended the meeting.

item.title: 23rd Presidential Election: EC seeks MPs' list from Parliament Secretariat
item.description:
The Election Commission (EC) has sought the list of Members of Parliament (MPs) from the Parliament Secretariat to prepare the electoral roll for the election of Bangladesh's 23rd President.
EC Senior Secretary Akhtar Ahmed said the date and schedule for the presidential election will be determined only after the voter list is received.
He made the remarks while speaking to reporters at the Election Bhaban in Agargaon, Dhaka, on Monday.
"No date or schedule for the presidential election has been fixed yet," he said. "We have requested the Parliament Secretariat to provide the electoral roll. Once we receive the voter list, we will discuss the election date and schedule."
Former President Mohammed Shahabuddin resigned on July 24, citing personal reasons. He submitted his resignation to the Speaker of Parliament through an official letter written on the President's letterhead, invoking Article 50(3) of the Constitution. He served as Bangladesh's 22nd President.
On the issue of National Identity (NID) card corrections, the EC secretary said a committee has been formed to review the matter, but its recommendations have yet to be finalised.
"The discussions have been held within a broad framework, but no standard operating procedure (SOP) has been finalised to define the issues the committee will examine and ensure there are no inconsistencies. I will brief the media on the matter in detail later," he said.
Explaining the hierarchy of official documents, he said the National Identity Card is Bangladesh's primary identity document, while a passport is a travel document.
"We rely on birth registration certificates issued by the Registrar General of Birth and Death Registration, while passport authorities rely on information contained in the NID," he added.

item.title: Two die of dengue in Sylhet, Khulna
item.description:
Two people died of dengue in Sylhet and Khulna over the last 24 hours until 8am on Monday.
Sylhet has recorded its first dengue-related death of this year after 54-year-old Afia Khanam died while undergoing treatment at Sylhet MAG Osmani Medical College Hospital. It is the first confirmed dengue fatality in the Sylhet division in 2026.
Assistant Director of the Sylhet Health Department, Dr. Nur-e-Alam Shamim, said the patient also suffered from heart disease and hypertension. He added that public awareness campaigns are being intensified to help prevent further infections.
According to the Health Department's daily dengue report released on Monday, two new dengue cases were confirmed in the past 24 hours, raising the total number of infections in the division to 111. One patient was diagnosed at Sylhet MAG Osmani Medical College Hospital and the other at Moulvibazar Sadar Hospital.
Currently, five dengue patients are receiving treatment at hospitals across the division. Since January 1, Sylhet has reported 24 cases, Sunamganj 21, Habiganj 52, and Moulvibazar 11, while three patients from other districts also received treatment in Sylhet division hospitals.
Besides, the death toll from dengue in Khulna Division has risen to 10 this year after one more patient died while undergoing treatment at Khulna Medical College Hospital, health officials said.
During the same period, 67 new dengue patients were admitted to hospitals, bringing the total number of patients currently receiving treatment across the division to 196, according to the latest report issued by Directorate of Health.
Dr. Sheikh Md. Mosharraf Hossain, Director (Health) of Khulna Division, said the new admissions included 14 in Khulna district, 26 at Khulna Medical College Hospital, two in Bagerhat, six in Jessore, three in Jhenaidah, five in Narail and one at Satkhira Medical College Hospital.
Between January 1 and August 3, a total of 2,219 dengue patients were hospitalized across the division. Of them, 1,988 have recovered and been discharged, while 25 were referred to other hospitals for advanced treatment.
Of the 10 dengue-related deaths recorded this year, nine occurred at Khulna Medical College Hospital, including three patients from Khulna, while one death was reported in Bagerhat.

item.title: Swapon: Strengthen parliamentary democracy to honour July martyrs
item.description:
Information and Broadcasting Minister Zahir Uddin Swapon on Monday said Bangladesh must strengthen its parliamentary democracy to truly honour the sacrifices of those martyred in the July Mass Uprising, stressing that the elected national parliament should remain the country's principal forum for political activity and policymaking.
Speaking at a discussion marking the July Mass Uprising Day at the National Press Club in Dhaka, the minister said all political disputes should be resolved through constitutional and democratic processes rather than outside parliament.
The programme was organised by the Bangladesh Federal Union of Journalists (BFUJ) and the Dhaka Union of Journalists (DUJ).
Swapon said it was both painful and a matter of national self-reflection that, more than five decades after achieving independence through the Liberation War, people once again had to sacrifice their lives to secure democracy and voting rights.
He said the public mandate delivered through the July Mass Uprising could only be fulfilled by making parliamentary democracy more effective and robust.
"The true value of the democracy achieved through so much bloodshed and sacrifice will be realised only when the National Parliament is established as the country's highest democratic platform for political debate, dialogue and decision-making," he said, adding that a civilised political culture is rooted in parliament-centric politics.
The minister said remembering the martyrs should not be limited to ceremonies or emotions, but should be reflected in efforts to strengthen democratic institutions. He called for keeping political disagreements within democratic norms and enriching the political process through greater public participation.
The minister said the Language Movement, the Liberation War and the July Mass Uprising represent a continuous struggle for democracy, and that the sacrifices made in each movement form part of the same historical legacy.
"The only way to repay the debt owed to those martyrs is to establish an effective parliament, an independent and dignified judiciary, good governance and a strong constitutional democracy," he said.
Swapon said these goals could not be achieved by any single political party alone and urged all democratic forces to work together. He emphasised that national unity, mutual cooperation and democratic tolerance are essential to fulfilling the aspirations of the July martyrs.
Referring to social media, the minister said it has become an important platform for political expression but warned that intolerance, misinformation and a culture of instability on such platforms could undermine democracy. He urged to uphold decency, reason and democratic values in expressing differing opinions.
The minister also said the government remains committed to implementing every pledge of the July Charter through the country's elected parliament.

item.title: Fakhrul: Govt not interfering in media
item.description:
BNP Secretary General and Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives Minister Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has said there is no government interference in the media.
"Rather, there is a tendency to create divisions among journalists and push one another aside," he said.
He made the remarks while speaking at a program jointly organised by the Bangladesh Federal Union of Journalists (BFUJ) and the Dhaka Union of Journalists (DUJ) at the National Press Club on Monday, marking the second anniversary of the July Movement.
Information and Broadcasting Minister Zahir Uddin Swapon and State Minister Yasser Khan Choudhury also addressed the event.
Fakhrul said transparency in the media required the appointment of qualified professionals.
"It is important to ensure that competent people are appointed in the media to maintain transparency," he said.
Referring to the July Charter, Fakhrul said a committee had already been formed to implement it.
"There are differing opinions on whether the issue requires reform or amendment. These matters should be discussed in parliament," he said.
He also urged political parties to avoid escalating disagreements.
"The opposition is speaking outside parliament in the same way Sheikh Hasina used to. We should not allow the situation to escalate into conflict," he said.

item.title: FFWC warns of fresh flood risks amid heavy monsoon rain across Bangladesh
item.description:
The Flood Forecasting and Warning Centre (FFWC) has warned of an increased risk of flooding in several northern, northeastern and southeastern districts as heavy to very heavy monsoon rainfall across Bangladesh, combined with intense precipitation in India's upstream catchments, continues to raise river levels.
According to the Flood Forecasting and Warning Centre under the Bangladesh Water Development Board (BWDB), data recorded until 9am on Monday showed widespread heavy rainfall across the country's northern, northeastern, central and southeastern regions.
Heavy rainfall was also recorded in the Indian states of Meghalaya, West Bengal and Arunachal Pradesh, raising concerns over rising flows in transboundary rivers.
Dalia in Nilphamari recorded the country's highest rainfall over the past 24 hours at 162mm, followed by Durgapur in Netrokona (150mm), Maheshkhola in Sunamganj (134mm) and Noakhali (102mm).
Other notable rainfall totals included Feni (81mm), Jariajanjail in Netrokona (75mm), Barguna (64mm), Narsingdi (57mm), Rajshahi (57mm), Senbagh in Noakhali (54mm), Rohanpur in Chapainawabganj (53mm) and Basurhat in Noakhali (50mm).
The widespread rainfall suggests the active monsoon is affecting multiple river basins simultaneously, increasing the risk of localized flooding in low-lying areas.
The FFWC also reported heavy rainfall across India's upstream catchments that feed several rivers flowing into Bangladesh.
Baghmara in Meghalaya recorded 107mm of rainfall over the past 24 hours, while Ratachera in Meghalaya received 73mm, Pasighat in Arunachal Pradesh recorded 60mm and Cooch Behar in West Bengal measured 56mm.
These areas are part of the catchments of several transboundary rivers that flow into Bangladesh. Water from upstream rainfall typically takes time to move downstream, meaning river levels in Bangladesh could continue rising even if rainfall eases locally.
While no widespread flooding has been reported so far, the FFWC said hydrological conditions point to an elevated flood risk over the coming days, particularly in low-lying floodplains, haor areas and riverside communities.
Districts along the Teesta, Dharla, Dudhkumar, Brahmaputra-Jamuna, Surma-Kushiyara and Feni river systems could see further rises in water levels if heavy rainfall persists both in Bangladesh and upstream in India.
Flash floods remain a particular concern in northeastern districts such as Sunamganj and Netrokona, where intense rainfall can inundate low-lying areas within a short period.
The FFWC said it is closely monitoring rainfall and river conditions and will issue updated forecasts and warnings as the situation evolves.

item.title: August 5 public holiday to be observed nationwide
item.description:
The government will observe a nationwide public holiday on August 5 to mark July Mass Uprising Day. The day was added to the official list of government holidays last year.
Government, semi-government and autonomous institutions will remain closed on the occasion.
However, officials and employees of essential and public service institutions will continue to perform their duties according to their designated duty rosters.
Essential services include hospitals and emergency healthcare, law enforcement agencies, Fire Service and Civil Defence, electricity, gas and water supply institutions, seaports and land ports, airports, Bangladesh Railway, road public transport, prisons, disaster management services and other essential government services.
According to the Ministry of Public Administration's 2026 government holiday calendar, August 5 falls on Wednesday. Government employees who take casual or optional leave on Thursday, August 6, will be able to enjoy a continuous 4-day break by combining it with the weekly holidays on Friday and Saturday.
Whether private sector banks, financial institutions, garment factories and other commercial establishments will remain closed on August 5 will be decided by the respective institutions in line with government directives and their own policies.
Last year, garment factories also observed a holiday on August 5. At the time, the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) said in a statement that the decision had been taken in solidarity with the government-declared public holiday and to pay tribute to those martyred on that day.
BGMEA has not yet announced any decision regarding factory operations on August 5 this year.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 847 as three die in 24 hours
item.description:
Three more children have died from measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am on Monday, raising the overall death toll from the ongoing outbreak to 847.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified all three of the latest casualties as suspected.
With the latest figures, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 751, while the number of confirmed deaths remained unchanged at 96, as no new confirmed measles deaths were reported in the last 24 hours.
Among the latest fatalities, the Sylhet division recorded the highest number of deaths, with two casualties reported in the Sunamganj district.
A total of 967 suspected measles cases were recorded in the 24 hours till Monday morning, taking the overall suspected case tally to 131,050.
During the same period, 113 new confirmed measles cases were reported, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 16,408.
Since March 15, 2026, a total of 113,528 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 109,189 have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, according to the DGHS.

item.title: Study rules out vaccine-resistant measles strain
item.description:
As Bangladesh battles its worst measles outbreak in decades, preliminary research has found no evidence that the virus has evolved to evade protection from the existing measles vaccine, easing fears that a vaccine-resistant strain is driving the epidemic.
Instead, researchers say the outbreak appears to be fueled by immunity gaps, with the youngest infants, too young to receive their first routine vaccine dose, and unvaccinated children accounting for the overwhelming majority of confirmed infections.
The findings, released by researchers from the International Centre for Diarrhoeal Disease Research, Bangladesh (icddr,b) and Bangladesh Shishu Hospital and Institute (BSH&I), come as the country continues to record thousands of infections and hundreds of deaths.
According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), Bangladesh reported 122,763 suspected measles cases and 15,272 laboratory-confirmed infections between March 15 and July 25 this year.
During the same period, 721 suspected and 95 laboratory-confirmed measles-related deaths were recorded.
The scale of the outbreak has prompted public concern that the virus may have mutated enough to render existing vaccines ineffective.
However, genomic sequencing and laboratory analysis found no evidence to support that belief.
Researchers identified the circulating virus as belonging to the B3 genotype, the same strain responsible for outbreaks in several other countries, and found no indication that it had genetically escaped vaccine-induced immunity.
“Our findings provide no evidence that the virus has escaped vaccine protection,” said Dr Noorjahan Maliha, associate scientist at icddr,b’s Virology Laboratory.
Although a small number of fully vaccinated children were infected, she said the hospital-based investigation was not designed to measure overall vaccine effectiveness and should not be interpreted as evidence that the vaccine is failing.
The investigation examined 341 children aged up to 14 years admitted with suspected measles to Bangladesh Shishu Hospital between April 20 and May 21.
Laboratory testing confirmed measles in 324 of them.
The highest infection rates were recorded among children with little or no vaccine protection.
Among infants younger than nine months, who are too young to receive Bangladesh’s first routine measles-rubella vaccine, 97% tested positive.
The same positivity rate was observed among eligible children who had received no vaccine.
The proportion gradually declined among vaccinated children.
It fell to 92% among those who had received one dose and 76% among those who had received both recommended doses.
Researchers stressed that these figures relate only to children already admitted to hospital with suspected measles and should not be interpreted as infection rates among all vaccinated children.
Instead, the progressively lower positivity among vaccinated children is consistent with the vaccine providing meaningful protection, although larger population-based studies will be required to determine precisely how effective it has been during the current outbreak.
The findings also highlight a critical period of vulnerability among infants.
Bangladesh administers the first routine measles-rubella vaccine at nine months and the second at 15 months.
Before that, babies rely largely on antibodies transferred from their mothers.
An initial analysis of stored blood samples from an earlier icddr,b birth cohort found maternal antibodies declined rapidly during the first months of life.
In the small group studied, no protective antibodies remained between three and eight months of age, suggesting many infants may become susceptible well before reaching the age for routine vaccination.
Researchers cautioned that the sample was too small for firm conclusions and said broader studies are underway.
Dr Mustafizur Rahman, senior director of icddr,b’s Infectious Diseases Division, said the findings suggest Bangladesh should focus less on fears of viral mutation and more on understanding why such a large outbreak occurred despite relatively high reported vaccination coverage.
“We need to determine why children miss vaccination and whether reported national coverage conceals communities with substantial immunity gaps,” he said.
icddr,b Executive Director Dr Tahmeed Ahmed said the institution has already expanded its research to examine why some vaccinated children became infected, how malnutrition may influence immune protection, why some patients develop severe disease and when infants lose maternal antibodies.
Researchers emphasized that the findings should reinforce, not weaken, public confidence in vaccination.
They urged parents not to delay immunisation and advised that all eligible children receive every recommended dose of the measles-rubella vaccine while continuing to follow government vaccination guidance during the ongoing outbreak.

item.title: Actor Zaher Alvi gets bail in wife's suicide abetment case
item.description:
The High Court has granted bail to actor Zaher Alvi, also known as Md Niamat Ullah Bhuiyan, in a case filed over the alleged abetment of his wife Afra Ibnath Khan Ikra’s suicide, clearing the way for his release from jail.
A High Court bench comprising Justice K M Zahid Sarwar and Justice Sheikh Abu Taher passed the order on Sunday after making absolute a previously issued rule on his bail.
Zaher Alvi was sent to jail on June 30 after being produced before a Dhaka court following a two-day remand. Police requested that he be kept in custody until the investigation was completed, and Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid granted the request.
Earlier, on June 18, the actor surrendered before the court of Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Kamal Uddin through his lawyer and sought bail. The court rejected his petition and ordered his imprisonment.
On June 21, the investigating officer sought a seven-day remand for further investigation. After a hearing on June 24, Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Al Biruni Mir granted a two-day remand.
According to the case statement, Ikra was found hanging at her residence in the Mirpur DOHS area of Dhaka on February 28. She was taken to Kurmitola General Hospital where doctors declared her dead.
The following day, her father Kabir Hayat Khan, filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, alleging that prolonged family disputes and sustained mental abuse had driven his daughter to take her own life.
Alvi and Ikra married in 2010 and have a son.

item.title: Detained Aung San Suu Kyi meets Red Cross delegate in Myanmar
item.description:
Myanmar’s detained democratic leader Aung San Suu Kyi met with the Red Cross representative to the country on Monday, the humanitarian group said, the first publicized meeting between her and a foreign official since she was ousted in a 2021 coup.
The military deposed Suu Kyi in February 2021, jailing the Nobel Peace Prize laureate and triggering an ongoing civil war that has killed more than 100,000 people, according to monitor Acled.
The coup leader and former junta chief, Min Aung Hlaing, was installed as civilian president in April following highly restricted elections.
Analysts say the vote -- which did not include Suu Kyi’s party -- was part of an effort to whitewash Min Aung Hlaing’s rule.
Suu Kyi’s son, Kim Aris, welcomed her meeting with the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), describing it on Monday as “an important first step” that brought hope.
Kim Aris, a British national, has sought independently verified proof that his mother is alive after she was transferred from prison to house arrest in April following Min Aung Hlaing’s change in position.
He said in a social media post he hoped the meeting would lead to “greater humanitarian access, direct contact with my mother, credible and independently verified information about her wellbeing, and ultimately her immediate and unconditional release, together with all political prisoners.”
An ICRC spokesperson told AFP that its resident representative to Myanmar, Arnaud de Baecque, visited Suu Kyi on Monday.
The visit included the opportunity to speak with Suu Kyi “in private,” the ICRC said in a statement.
The Myanmar president’s office earlier announced the meeting, releasing photos of Suu Kyi shaking hands and sitting with de Baecque.
The ICRC spokesperson confirmed the veracity of the two images, and said the group did not take them.
Suu Kyi, now 81, was moved to house arrest after Min Aung Hlaing said he had commuted the rest of her sentence.
She was detained on a host of charges that rights groups say were confected to sideline her and her popular National League for Democracy party.
“We are happy to see her photo like this if it’s really her meeting with the ICRC. We can know now that she’s alive,” a veteran politician of her party told AFP on condition of anonymity before the ICRC confirmed the visit.
“However, Aunty should be released immediately as she’s being detained unlawfully,” the politician said.
Authorities have not disclosed the exact location of Suu Kyi’s detention in the capital Naypyidaw, nor how many years of her sentence remain.
The ICRC did not share her location, nor details of her health condition, noting that under its working methods, the organization’s observations related to visits with detainees are only shared with the detaining authorities.
Myanmar has been largely ostracized by the international community since the coup, but analysts say Min Aung Hlaing is seeking to secure international legitimacy.
The 11-nation Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) has excluded member state Myanmar’s leadership from high-level summits.
However, neighbor Thailand has been leading an effort to bring Myanmar back into the diplomatic fold, bilaterally and through the regional bloc.
Min Aung Hlaing has travelled to India, China and Asean member Laos since becoming president, and he is scheduled to make an official visit to Thailand this week.
“It’s the old military game plan to use Suu Kyi as a bargaining chip,” independent Myanmar analyst David Mathieson told AFP.
Some Asean nations have long called for proof of life, Mathieson said, adding that the timing of the government-permitted meeting between Suu Kyi and the ICRC representative -- days before Min Aung Hlaing’s trip to Bangkok -- was no coincidence.
“As a gesture to the international community, it’s the wildcard Min Aung Hlaing was holding close to his chest,” he said.
The Myanmar government could “gain a lot from Asean” by permitting access to Suu Kyi, said Myanmar specialist Morgan Michaels.
“Releasing her in particular would go a long way to facilitating Myanmar’s re-invitation at the political level,” Michaels said.
Suu Kyi’s continued detention remains a major sticking point for some despite Myanmar’s recent diplomatic outreach.
Asean has pressed for its special envoy to meet Suu Kyi, but Myanmar has so far refused.

To promote the adoption of Bangla QR, raise public awareness of secure and cashless transactions, and further strengthen the country's digital payment ecosystem, Al-Arafah Islami Bank PLC launched the Bangla QR & Digital Dan Box Acquiring Excellence Campaign 2026 and organized a Bangla QR Awareness Rally.

Chairman of the board of directors Badiur Rahman, and chairman of the executive committee of the board Salim Rahman were present as special guests.
The program was presided over by managing director of the bank Mohd Rafat Ullah Khan.
Deputy managing director & head of digital banking division Md Aminul Islam Bhuiyan was also present.
The event was conducted by SEVP & head of GSD Engr Md Habib Ullah.

They later led an awareness rally joined by the Bank's executives and employees.
The rally started from the corporate head office premises, marched through the surrounding streets, and concluded at the same venue.
Md Sarwar Hossain, deputy governor of Bangladesh Bank, emphasized that the widespread adoption of Bangla QR is essential to ensuring secure, fast, and convenient digital transactions.
He underscored the importance of collaborative efforts among banks, merchants, and customers in advancing the country's vision of a Smart Bangladesh and a cashless economy.
Speaking at the event, Badiur Rahman, chairman of the board of directors of Al-Arafah Islami Bank PLC, said that Bangla QR is more than just a payment solution; it is an effective tool for expanding digital financial inclusion and promoting cashless transactions.
He stressed the need for continuous awareness initiatives to encourage greater adoption of Bangla QR among merchants and the general public.
Mohd Rafat Ullah Khan, managing director & CEO of Al-Arafah Islami Bank PLC, said that the Bank remains committed to delivering secure, convenient, and Shariah-compliant digital banking services.
He added that the Bank's digital initiatives, including Bangla QR, Digital Dan Box, Islamic Wallet, Internet Banking, and IlmNet, will further accelerate cashless transactions and strengthen financial inclusion across the country.
Among others, the bank's senior executives, heads of various divisions, and officials participated in the program.
Through the campaign and awareness rally, the bank reaffirmed its commitment to promoting the widespread adoption of Bangla QR, encouraging secure digital payments, and contributing to the development of a modern, inclusive, and cashless digital economy in Bangladesh.

Humaiun Kobir: Bangladesh well-placed for regional connectivity
item.description:
Emphasising the growing importance of regional connectivity, Prime Minister's Foreign Affairs Adviser Humaiun Kobir on Monday said investments in transport infrastructure, aviation and digital networks are key drivers of economic growth and stronger people-to-people contacts.
"Bangladesh's strategic location provides significant opportunities to strengthen regional connectivity and expand cooperation in trade, tourism, investment and cultural exchanges," he said, noting that Bangladesh welcome greater collaboration with China and other international partners in advancing sustainable infrastructure, aviation, tourism and innovation for the benefit of the people.
Speaking as the chief guest at a joint training session's opening ceremony in the capital, the adviser stressed that future prosperity will depend not only on economic success but also on the quality of institutions, social resilience and international cooperation.
The Bangladesh Institute of International and Strategic Studies (BIISS) hosted the joint training program titled "2026 Comparative Governance Forum" at the BIISS Auditorium.
"The countries of the Global South are becoming increasingly influential in shaping global governance and sustainable development," Kobir said.
He said Bangladesh believes the international system must be more inclusive, rules-based and responsive to the aspirations of all nations. "We support multilateralism, peaceful dialogue and international cooperation as the most effective means of addressing common global challenges."
The adviser said lasting progress is achieved when nations invest in knowledge, trust and partnerships built on mutual respect.
"Economic growth creates prosperity, but wisdom, cooperation and mutual understanding are what ultimately secure peace and sustainable development," he said.
Prof Chen Zhimin, Vice-President of Fudan University, and Yao Wen, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of the People's Republic of China to the People's Republic of Bangladesh, attended the opening ceremony of the joint training program as special guests.
The adviser underscored the importance of deepening Bangladesh-China cooperation through knowledge sharing, dialogue and mutual learning, saying stronger partnerships are essential to addressing increasingly complex global challenges.
He said the initiative reflects the shared commitment of both countries to strengthening academic and institutional cooperation.
"I would like to acknowledge the valuable support of the Embassy of the People's Republic of China and all our partner institutions. This forum reflects our shared belief that dialogue, knowledge and mutual learning remain indispensable in addressing the increasingly complex challenges of our time," he said.
The adviser said Bangladesh has much to learn from China's development experience while also sharing its own strengths in public policy and governance.
"Comparative governance calls for a comparative perspective on the governance systems of both countries. We can learn tremendously from the People's Republic of China. At the same time, there are areas where Bangladesh has performed well, and we should continue to build on those achievements," he said.
Describing China as one of the world's most remarkable development success stories, the adviser noted that the country has lifted around 800 million people out of extreme poverty over the past four decades through sustained reforms and economic transformation.
"China is a tremendous example of development over the last four decades. It has lifted nearly 800 million people out of extreme poverty through one of the most successful poverty alleviation programmes in history and has implemented major market reforms that have transformed its economy," he said.
At the same time, Kobir said Bangladesh has earned international recognition in several important areas, particularly disaster risk reduction and climate resilience.
"Bangladesh has become internationally recognised for reducing disaster risks and protecting lives. However, climate change is a global challenge that requires global solutions. We must continue to advocate for stronger multilateral cooperation, enhanced climate finance, technology transfer and greater support for vulnerable developing countries," he said.
Expressing optimism about the program, he said the discussions over the coming days would generate new ideas, strengthen academic and institutional cooperation and further reinforce the enduring friendship between Bangladesh and China.
Director General of BIISS Major General Ridwanur Rahman also spoke.

item.title: PM appeals for public help to keep Bangladesh clean and litter-free
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Monday sought people's cooperation in keeping Bangladesh clean and protecting the environment, urging everyone to refrain from littering and dispose of waste responsibly to help build a cleaner and better more liveable country for future generations.
In a video message posted on his verified Facebook page, the prime minister said protecting the environment is not solely the government's responsibility but a shared duty of every citizen.
“If each of us becomes more conscious from today and disposes of our waste in designated places properly instead of throwing it indiscriminately, we can gradually make Bangladesh free of waste and build a beautiful environment,” he said.
Tarique Rahman said Bangladesh belongs to all its people and stressed that if everyone makes even a small contribution, the country would be able to achieve significant progress together.
"I seek your cooperation. Let us all work together to keep our country clean and beautiful. Let each of us do our part to protect and preserve a clean environment that will ensure a healthier, more liveable country for future generations,” Tarique Rahman said.
He said environmental cleanliness is an issue that touches people from all walks of life, as everyone is affected by the condition of their surroundings.

item.title: Oil prices fall nearly 5% after US announces new Iran talks
item.description:
Oil prices tumbled on Monday in early Asia trade after US President Donald Trump announced fresh talks with Iran to end the Middle East war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
The war, which began in late February when the United States and Israel attacked Iran, has caused oil prices to swing sharply as it effectively closed the waterway, a vital route for global oil and gas supplies.
At around 2250 GMT on Sunday, the price of a barrel of Brent North Sea, the benchmark international oil contract, for September delivery was down 4.69% at $83.81.
Its American equivalent, West Texas Intermediate, fell 4.67% to $80.72.
Trump said on Sunday that fresh negotiations with Iran will begin on Monday after holding off on major strikes against the Islamic republic to pursue a deal.
"Now what we're doing is we're talking to them in the form of a negotiation. It begins tomorrow afternoon," he said, without providing further details of the venue of the talks or the participants.
Hours after the US had called off major strikes Iran on Sunday said it was nearing a deal with Oman over a new route through the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Study: 9 in 10 families borrow for measles treatment
item.description:
Nearly nine in 10 families affected by measles in Bangladesh have had to borrow money to cover treatment costs, while six in 10 depleted their savings, according to a joint assessment by the Bangladesh Red Crescent Society (BDRCS) and the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC).
The assessment found that 89% of affected families borrowed money to pay for treatment, while 61% used up their savings.
Every family surveyed said they required financial assistance. Among them, 35% identified medicines as their top priority, followed by water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) support (33%) and food assistance (22%). Around 4% reported selling assets, while 3% relied on donations.
The assessment covered 2,746 measles-affected households receiving treatment at 12 government medical college and district hospitals across Bangladesh.
It found that the outbreak's financial impact extended well beyond medical expenses. Around 75% of patients were aged four years or below, 19% were between five and 17 years, and 6% were aged 18 or above.
The assessment was conducted to identify 2,400 of the most vulnerable households for emergency cash assistance of Tk10,000 each and to evaluate the socio-economic impact of the outbreak. Of the 2,746 households assessed, 2,400 were selected to receive assistance based on agreed vulnerability criteria.
According to the findings, affected families spent an average of Tk16,000 on treatment and related expenses. Many caregivers also reported losing income or even their jobs after spending extended periods in hospitals caring for sick family members.
Hazera Khatun travelled from Rangpur to Dhaka with her 11-month-old daughter, who is receiving treatment at Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital. The family has already spent more than Tk70,000.
"Treatment at the government hospital is free, but many other costs are not covered," she said.
"We spent nearly Tk20,000 just to reach Dhaka by ambulance. Every day we have to buy food, pay for medical tests and meet other daily expenses. I have already borrowed money from relatives. My husband works in Saudi Arabia, but he has not received his salary this month, making the situation even more difficult."
Among respondents who disclosed their occupations, 78% depended on informal employment and earned between Tk6,000 and Tk20,000 per month, making them particularly vulnerable to income loss during prolonged illness.
Dr Kabir M Ashraf Alam, secretary general of BDRCS, said the findings showed that many families were facing both a health emergency and severe financial hardship.
"Through our emergency response, we are providing cash assistance to the most vulnerable households while continuing community awareness activities," he said.
Alberto Bocanegra, head of delegation of the IFRC in Bangladesh, said the consequences of the measles outbreak extended beyond hospital treatment.
"Families often face serious financial hardship while caring for sick children or other family members. These findings highlight why humanitarian assistance and strong social protection systems are essential during public health emergencies. It is important that our response is guided by evidence," he said.
With support from the IFRC and its partners, BDRCS has assisted the government in implementing the nationwide measles vaccination campaign. The organisation has also mobilised more than 1,000 Red Crescent volunteers to conduct community awareness campaigns, support vaccination centres, and promote risk communication and early healthcare seeking.

item.title: All staff of Kashimpur land office suspended over irregularities
item.description:
All officials and employees of the Kashimpur Union Land Office have been suspended after prima facie evidence of various irregularities was found during a sudden inspection.

item.title: Pregnant woman dies after alleged assault by husband in Dhamrai
item.description:
A three-month pregnant woman died after allegedly being beaten by her husband in Dhamrai, Dhaka. Police have arrested the accused, Liton Sarkar.
The incident occurred in the Gomgram area of Jadabpur Union on Sunday.
Police recovered the body at night and sent it to the morgue of Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital in Dhaka for an autopsy.
According to police and local sources, Liton Sarkar works as a CNG auto-rickshaw driver.
Family members alleged that he had long been addicted to drugs and regularly subjected his wife, Popi Rani Sarkar, 27, to physical and mental abuse.
They alleged that Liton beat Popi with a stick during a family dispute on Sunday afternoon in front of their seven-year-old child, leaving her critically injured and unconscious.
Later in the evening, he, with the help of locals, took her to Kalampur Holy General Hospital, where the on-duty doctor declared her dead.

Dhaka air quality moderate Monday morning
item.description:
The air quality in Dhaka remained moderate on Monday morning, with an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 79 at 8am.
With the score, the capital ranked 19th among the world's most polluted cities.
Uganda's Kampala, Pakistan's Lahore and Bahrain's Manama occupied the top three spots on the list, with AQI scores of 158, 154 and 147, respectively.
An AQI score between 50 and 100 is considered "moderate" with an acceptable air quality, while one between 101 and 150 is considered "unhealthy for sensitive groups", while a score between 151 and 200 is classified as "unhealthy."
AQI readings between 201 and 300 are termed "very unhealthy", and anything above 301 is considered "hazardous", posing serious health risks.
The AQI is a daily indicator of air quality, showing how clean or polluted the air is and the possible health effects people may experience.
In Bangladesh, the AQI is calculated based on five major pollutants: particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide, carbon monoxide, sulphur dioxide and ozone.

Three Chinese, Bangladeshi woman held over online fraud, illegal VoIP operation
item.description:
Detectives have arrested three Chinese nationals and a Bangladeshi woman for allegedly operating a sophisticated online fraud, illegal Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) and online gambling network from a rented building in the capital's Bashundhara Residential Area.
Speaking at a press briefing at the DMP Media Centre on Sunday, DB Chief Shafiqul Islam said the four suspects were arrested during a raid carried out by the Cyber Crime Division of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP)'s Detective Branch (DB) in Bashundhara Residential Area on Saturday night.
The arrestees were identified as Jharna Chakma Ziana, 27, Liu Hui Zhang, 46, Wei Yuji, 30, and She Yi Ran, 42.
According to investigators, the suspects had set up their operation on the fourth and fifth floors of a six-storey building in Bashundhara, using advanced digital technology to conduct illegal VoIP activities, online gambling and cyber fraud.
During the raid, detectives seized 14 laptops, 16 smartphones, more than 6,000 SIM cards of various mobile operators, 20 SIM gateway devices, 26 bottles of foreign liquor and Tk 209,700 in cash.
DB officials said Jharna rented the entire building before subletting the fourth and fifth floors to the Chinese nationals, who allegedly used the premises as a base for their illegal operations.
According to the investigation, the syndicate targeted victims by sending text messages offering fake job opportunities, attractive promotional deals and easy income schemes. Recipients who clicked the embedded links were allegedly drawn into fraudulent online platforms and deceived into transferring money.
Police said the group employed sophisticated technology to evade detection, including SIM gateway devices that enabled a single mobile handset to operate up to 12 SIM cards simultaneously. The system made it difficult for investigators to immediately trace the International Mobile Equipment Identity (IMEI) numbers of the devices, even after victims lodged complaints.
DB officials alleged that the network defrauded members of the public of millions of taka, which was subsequently laundered abroad through the organised cybercrime operation.
Legal proceedings against the four accused are underway.

Centuries-old bamboo craft fights for survival in Dinajpur
item.description:
The centuries-old tradition of bamboo craft in the northern district Dinajpur is fast fading, as modern lifestyles, high prices and declining demand drive artisans away from their ancestral trade.
A visit to the traditional Setabganj market in Bochaganj upazila found artisans grappling with shrinking demand, soaring bamboo prices and limited market access, leaving many unable to recover even their production costs.
As earnings continue to decline, a growing number of craftsmen are abandoning their ancestral profession for day labour, farming and battery-powered three-wheeler driving.
"We once made a decent living from bamboo work. Now it is no longer enough to support a family, and our children have no interest in continuing the trade," said veteran artisan Biplab Pal, who has been engaged in the craft for nearly 40 years.
Long-time craftsmen Mahesh Chandra Roy and Anil Pal shared similar concerns, saying they continue the profession largely to preserve a family tradition despite earning only nominal profits.
Another artisan, Nikhil Sarkar, said financial hardship forced him to steer his eldest son into another occupation.
Yet amid the industry's decline, a handful of craftsmen are finding new opportunities through innovation.
Artisan Shafiqul Islam has introduced colourful finishes and contemporary designs to traditional bamboo products, helping attract younger buyers and improve sales.
"Customers now prefer modern-looking products. By redesigning traditional bamboo items, I've been able to increase both demand and profits," he said.
Young entrepreneur Arif Hossain said bamboo craftsmanship represents an important part of Bangladesh's cultural heritage and should be preserved through better planning, modern product development and stronger government support.
Artisans and local stakeholders recommend design and skills training, easy-access loans for small producers and expanded commercial bamboo cultivation to ensure a stable supply of raw materials.
Deputy General Manager of the Bangladesh Small and Cottage Industries Corporation (BSCIC) in Dinajpur, Md Jahedul Islam, said modernization is key to reviving the sector.
He said BSCIC provides three-month training programmes to enhance artisans' skills, along with loan facilities and regular monitoring to help make bamboo-based enterprises commercially sustainable.
Without effective policy support and sustained institutional backing, artisans fear Dinajpur's once-thriving bamboo craft industry could soon become little more than a fading memory.

item.title: Bangladesh launches action plan to advance safe, orderly migration
item.description:
The government of Bangladesh, in collaboration with the International Organization for Migration (IOM), officially launched the National Action Plan (NAP) 2026-2030 to implement the objectives of the Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration (GCM) in Dhaka on Sunday.
The event was convened by the Co-Chairs of the Bangladesh Migration Compact Taskforce (BMCT) - the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Ministry of Expatriates’ Welfare and Overseas Employment, in coordination with IOM.
The European Union supported the development process of the NAP through the EU-funded Prottasha II project, implemented by IOM.
The event also included a debriefing on the outcomes of the International Migration Review Forum (IMRF) 2026, highlighting Bangladesh’s leadership and contributions to the global migration agenda.
The National Action Plan was approved by the Cabinet on May 21, 2026.
Mr Ariful Haque Choudhury, MP, minister, Ministry of Expatriates’ Welfare and Overseas Employment, graced the occasion as the chief guest.
Shama Obaed Islam, MP, state minister, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, chaired the occasion.
Md Nurul Haque, MP, state minister, Ministry of Expatriates’ Welfare and Overseas Employment; Mahdi Amin, adviser to the prime minister, Ugochi Daniels, deputy director general for Operations of the International Organization for Migration, attended the event as special guests.
Asad Alam Siam, foreign secretary and Md Mokhtar Ahmed, secretary, Ministry of Expatriates’ Welfare and Overseas Employment, as the Co-Chairs of the BMCT, delivered remarks on the NAP and their reflections on the 2026 IMRF.
The speakers, emphasizing sustained collaboration among government institutions, international partners, civil society, the private sector and migrants for the successful implementation of the NAP, underscored the Government’s commitment to ensuring that migration remains safe, orderly and regular while maximizing its contribution to national development and protecting the rights and dignity of Bangladeshi migrants.
The event also featured Bangladesh’s renewed commitments and pledges towards the implementation of the GCM, remarks from the civil society, and the official unveiling of the National Action Plan. Bangladesh’s GCM journey, achievements and challenges were showcased at the venue through a video documentary and a thematic exhibition.

item.title: Swapon: Truth, objectivity cornerstones of responsible journalism
item.description:
Information and Broadcasting Minister Zahir Uddin Swapon on Sunday said truth-seeking and objectivity are the cornerstones of responsible journalism, stressing that public service can only be achieved through rigorous fact-checking and impartial reporting.
Speaking as the chief guest at a seminar marking the 64th founding anniversary of the Department of Mass Communication and Journalism at the University of Dhaka, he said journalism risks losing its credibility when the pursuit of truth is influenced by preconceived positions or ideological bias.
"Journalists must place the pursuit of truth above all else and ensure the accuracy and objectivity of the information they present," he said.
The seminar, titled "The Interconnection of Politics, Power and Journalism: Theory, Reality and the Future," was held at the Professor Muzaffar Ahmed Chowdhury Auditorium of the university's Faculty of Social Sciences, according to Information Ministry Public Relations Officer Imranul Hasan. New Age Editor Nurul Kabir delivered the keynote address.
Swapon said the challenge today is no longer a lack of information but an overwhelming flood of content, where misinformation, disinformation and deliberate manipulation have emerged as serious threats to democracy, governance and society.
"In this environment, journalism's foremost responsibility is to verify facts, uncover the truth and present it to the public with objectivity," he said.
Describing journalism as more than a profession of reporting facts, the minister said it is one of the strongest pillars of public accountability, adding that no democratic state can be strengthened without a free, responsible and independent media.
He also underscored the need to ensure journalists' professional security, economic dignity and an enabling environment for independent reporting, while calling for greater professional capacity to counter misinformation.
During the question-and-answer session, Swapon said defining the limits of freedom of expression is inherently complex, as people express opinions from diverse political, philosophical and ideological perspectives.
However, he stressed that freedom must always be exercised with responsibility.
The minister said the government has initiated efforts to establish a Media Commission aimed at maintaining a balance between power, freedom and accountability.
"We want to establish a participatory and balanced Media Commission through consultations with all stakeholders to ensure harmony among power, freedom and responsibility," he said.
Earlier, Swapon reminisced about his student days at the University of Dhaka, describing his time on campus as one of the most cherished periods of his life and saying that returning to the university evoked a deep sense of nostalgia.
The seminar was chaired by Professor Kazi Mohammad Mahbubur Rahman, chairman of the Department of Mass Communication and Journalism, and moderated by Professor Robayet Ferdous.
University of Dhaka Vice-Chancellor Professor A B M Obaidul Islam attended as the special guest.

item.title: Home Ministe: Govt to build police force free from political influence
item.description:
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed on Sunday said the police must not serve as an instrument of any political party or group but should instead become a true friend of people and a symbol of public security.
The government's priority is to ensure public safety and build a modern, professional and people-oriented police force free from political influence, he said while addressing the graduation parade of the first phase of the 27th BCS (Police) batch at the Bangladesh Police Academy in Sardah, Rajshahi.
He said the government has taken various steps to restore the morale of the police force which was undermined by excessive politicisation during the previous “fascist government”.
The minister said a strict system of rewards for professionalism and disciplinary action for misconduct has been introduced to strengthen integrity and discipline within the force.
Congratulating the newly appointed officers who took part in the parade, the minister said this joyous moment should have come much earlier in their lives. He said it was deeply painful that they had endured 18 years of severe deprivation and inhumane suffering as victims of the vindictive actions of the previous authoritarian and fascist government.
The minister extended his heartfelt greetings to all the officers for regaining their rightful positions and due recognition following the fall of the authoritarian regime.
He said they were beginning their careers at a historic time for the country and urged them to uphold equality before the law.
“From political activists to marginal farmers, everyone is equal in the eyes of the law. No one seeking police services should face discrimination,” he added.
He also stressed the importance of maintaining the chain of command, discipline, loyalty and teamwork, while urging the officers to enhance their expertise in cyber security and criminal investigation to meet emerging challenges.
Reaffirming the government's zero-tolerance policy against corruption, Salahuddin called on all police members to perform their duties with honesty and dedication.
The minister expressed hope that members of the 27th BCS (Police) batch would use their knowledge and experience gained over the past 18 years in different professions to strengthen the Bangladesh Police.
A total of 58 probationary ASPs — 57 from the first phase of the 27th BCS (Police) batch and one from the 28th batch — officially entered service through the parade.
At the ceremony, Probationary ASP Dr Md Nurul Huda Bhuiyan won the Best in Field Activities award and was also named the Best Probationer. Probationary ASP ABM Mamun received the Best Shooter award, while Abu Numan Mohammad Khairul Islam won the Best Academic Award.
During the ceremony, the minister inspected the parade, took the salute and distributed awards among the best-performing probationary officers.
The event was attended as special guests by Land Minister Mizanur Rahman Minu, local Members of Parliament, Inspector General of Police (IGP) Md. Ali Hossain Fakir, Principal of Bangladesh Police Academy G M Azizur Rahman, Rajshahi Divisional Commissioner Dr. A.N.M. Bazlur Rashid, and Rajshahi Range Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Md. Ashik Saeed.
Senior military and civilian officials, local and foreign invited guests, guardians of the ASP probationers, and journalists from various media outlets were also present at the ceremony.

item.title: DB chief: Police tighten security for official vehicles over sabotage threat
item.description:
Bangladesh Police tightened security for official vehicles nationwide on Saturday following intelligence reports of possible sabotage, Detective Branch (DB) Chief of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Md Shafiqul Islam said on Sunday.
The clarification came on Sunday after journalists asked the DB Chief about the nationwide highest alert issued by Police Headquarters a day earlier.
Speaking at a press briefing at the DMP Media Centre, Shafiqul Islam said the directive was purely precautionary and aimed at ensuring the safety of police personnel and official vehicles.
"Recent bomb-related incidents and attempts to spread panic prompted senior officers to instruct field units to exercise greater vigilance," he said.
He added that police officers are responsible for safeguarding both themselves and government assets, and the latest directive simply reinforces existing security protocols.
"We are always alert. In light of the recent bomb scares, we have further strengthened our vigilance," the DB chief said.
On Saturday, Police Headquarters issued a nationwide highest alert after intelligence agencies warned of possible attacks on police vehicles, including jeeps, pickups and buses, by extremist members or other miscreants. Following the warning, all metropolitan, range, district and specialised police units were instructed to immediately tighten security.
The emergency directive stressed that there should be no lapse in ensuring the security of police vehicles, whether on duty or parked after duty hours.
It instructed officers to park vehicles only in secure locations during temporary stops and ensure they remain under constant supervision. Police vehicles must not be left unattended or without the designated driver or responsible officer under any circumstances.
The directive also called for enhanced security for all government vehicles stationed at police stations, police lines, office compounds and other designated facilities after duty hours. It further instructed units to intensify patrols, strengthen surveillance and remain alert to any suspicious persons or objects.
Describing the matter as "highly important," Police Headquarters directed all metropolitan, range, district and specialised units to strictly implement the security measures.

item.title: Brac Bank's CORPnet records highest-ever monthly transaction volume of nearly Tk30,000cr
item.description:
Brac Bank's corporate internet banking platform, CORPnet, recorded its highest-ever monthly transaction volume in June 2026, processing nearly Tk30,000 crore as businesses increasingly embraced digital transaction banking.
Building on its record monthly performance, CORPnet processed more than Tk143,000 crore in transactions during the first six months of 2026.
This was 40% higher than the Tk102,000 crore processed during the same period last year.
The growth reflects the accelerating digitalization of corporate banking in Bangladesh.
During the first half of 2026, digital channels accounted for 80% of Brac Bank's corporate transactions, up from 74% a year earlier.
The platform also continued to attract more business users.
The number of corporate client groups using CORPnet increased by 40% year on year, while the total number of transactions rose by 43% to 5.24 million during the first six months of the year, highlighting deeper engagement with the bank's digital transaction banking platform.
Beyond transaction growth, CORPnet also strengthened its commercial proposition through the introduction of new digital capabilities.
Recently launched features such as A-Challan, A4 Cheque Printing and Pay Order Issuance have expanded the platform's value proposition for corporate clients.
The platform now also enables corporates to pay Titas utility bills digitally in real time, reducing reliance on manual processes and branch visits.
Its collection solution through Virtual Accounts recorded 20% year-on-year growth in collection volume during the first half of 2026, helping businesses automate receivables reconciliation, accelerate collections, and improve working capital management.
Commenting on the milestone, Md Shaheen Iqbal, additional managing director and head of wholesale banking at Brac Bank, said: "The record transaction volume demonstrates how rapidly businesses are adopting digital banking to manage their day-to-day financial operations. At Brac Bank, we continue to invest in technology and innovation to deliver secure, efficient and scalable transaction banking solutions that help our clients operate with greater speed, control and convenience."
CORPnet is Brac Bank's corporate internet banking platform that enables businesses to manage payments, collections, liquidity and other banking transactions through a secure digital interface.

item.title: Experts urge withdrawal of proposal to raise foreign ownership cap in logistics
item.description:
Policymakers, entrepreneurs and researchers have called for the withdrawal of a proposal in the draft Freight Forwarding Rules to raise the foreign ownership ceiling from 40% to 49%.
The call came at a roundtable, "Protecting Domestic Investment in Logistics & Policy Reform", organized by the Center for Strategic Research (CSR) at the Brac Centre in Mohakhali, Dhaka, on Wednesday.
Zonayed Saki, State Minister for Planning, joined online as chief guest; Mahmudur Rahman Manna, president of Nagorik Oikya, attended as special guest.
The concept paper was presented by Saqeeb Anwer, executive director of CSR.
He said freight forwarding, shipping agency, customs agency and courier-express require little fixed capital to operate. Foreign ownership therefore brings no factories, equipment or technology — only a licence, through which existing cargo flows shift into the owner's own global network. What takes place in the market, he said, is substitution rather than competition.
The paper noted that Bangladesh spends at least $9 billion a year on freight, of which domestic vessels capture only 8% to 10%; with a larger fleet, around $2 billion could be retained onshore. After the Bangladesh Flag Vessels (Protection of Interest) Act 2019, the domestic ocean-going flag fleet grew from 48 vessels to 80.
Section 9(4) of the Civil Aviation Act 2017, which requires a foreign airline's agent to be wholly owned by a Bangladeshi citizen, has built a fully domestic GSA industry. Saqeeb Anwer said that although many wholly foreign-owned companies operate here, none has invested in a domestic vessel or in infrastructure.
Concern was expressed that the Shipping Agent and C&F Agent Licensing Rules have both cut the 60/40 structure to 51/49; that the current budget has withdrawn the 49% cap on ICDs and off-docks; and that courier services carry no cap at all.
The 60/40 structure in the freight forwarding rules is therefore the last remaining benchmark for domestic ownership.
The validity of licence renewals for wholly foreign-owned companies is also pending before the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 12489/2019; amending the rules before the rule nisi is disposed of could render the proceedings ineffective, speakers said.
Describing logistics as a sensitive sector tied to national security, Fazle Huda, MP for Naogaon-3, said many foreign firms take large sums of foreign exchange out of the country merely by issuing bills of lading and other documents, without visible infrastructure.
"We are not against foreign investment," he said. "But that investment must go into infrastructure — railways, cold chain, modern trucks and agriculture-based supply systems." Citing restrictions in Sri Lanka and India, he said a sector tied to trade, ports and internal security must be treated as strategic, and that the practice of running businesses behind nominal local partners arranged through lawyers or consultants must end.
Kabir Ahmed, president of IAEAB and adviser to BAFFA, said around 80% of the country's freight business is controlled by foreign firms, yet most bring no meaningful FDI.
Md Ariful Ahsan, president of Baffa, warned that continued over-dependence would weaken the domestic logistics industry.
Shafiqul Alam, editor of Daily Waadaa, said global realities and geopolitics must inform how foreign investment is sought, and that it may not be necessary in every sector.
Mahmudur Rahman Manna said excessive foreign participation is depriving domestic entrepreneurs of opportunity, and that the concealment in this sector needs far more open discussion.
ATM Azizul Akil David, former senior vice president of the Bangladesh China Chamber of Commerce and Industry, said effective interest rates reaching 23% to 24% are forcing domestic entrepreneurs out of business while foreign firms enjoy a comparative advantage.
Six demands were placed from the roundtable: a uniform 60/40 structure across all four sub-sectors, with domestic majority applied to shares, dividend rights and board voting; uniform and strict enforcement of existing rules at renewal; a minimum paid-up capital of $5 to $10 million for firms with foreign participation, of which at least 40% must be shown within 24 months as real investment in warehousing, equipment and transport fleet; foreign hiring limited to senior management; assessment of foreign exchange outflow as a precondition of licence renewal; and mandatory declaration of beneficial ownership to curb nominee holdings.
Also taking part were Abu Alam Md Shahid Khan, former secretary; Barrister M Saquibuzzaman; Mahmud Hosain, former vice president of ICAB, Hasan Mamun, consulting editor of Dhaka Stream; and Kamruzzaman, head of finance at Rifline Logistics.

item.description:
A Chittagong court on Sunday placed listed top criminal Mobarak Hossain Emon alias David Emon, and his three associates on 10 days' remand in murder and arms cases filed at Fatikchhari Police Station in Chattogram.
Judge of the Senior Judicial Magistrate-3 Motasim Billah passed the order when police produced the four accused before his court, seeking seven days' remand in each of the two cases.
The other accused placed on remand are Md Shamim, Safayet Hossain and Al Islam Alif, also known as Tamal.
After hearing both sides, the court granted five days' remand in each case, totalling 10 days.
On Thursday, another Chittagong court sent David Emon and three associates to jail after showing them arrested in three cases.
David Emon was arrested in a joint operation in Jessore in the early hours of July 29 while trying to flee to India.
Earlier in the day, the accused were produced before the court under tight security. Additional police were deployed in and around the court premises during the remand hearing.
According to case documents, police recovered firearms from Fatikchhari on July 29 based on information obtained from Emon and three others following their arrest.
Police said David Emon, 25, son of late Md Musa of Kanchannagar in Fatikchhari upazila, faces 13 cases, including those related to murder and illegal arms.
Additional Superintendent of Police (Hathazari Circle) Kazi Md Tareq Aziz said the accused will be questioned to gather further information about their criminal activities and to recover more illegal weapons.
According to multiple district police sources, investigators traced David Emon's whereabouts while probing the murder of Maksudul Haque Chowdhury in the Pahartali area on June 13.

No respite for Dhaka consumers as food prices soar
item.description:
As households struggle to cope with rising living costs, there is little sign of relief in Dhaka's kitchen markets, where the prices of rice, vegetables, fish, eggs and poultry continue to edge higher.
After visiting several kitchen markets across Dhaka on Saturday, it was found that, except for a few varieties, almost all vegetables were selling for around Tk100 per kg, while green chilli prices had soared to Tk400 per kg.
Rice prices have also resumed their upward trend, with polao rice registering the sharpest increase. Traders said its price has jumped by Tk50–60 per kg within just a few days, adding to the burden on consumers already coping with a gas supply crisis.
According to traders, persistent rainfall and flooding in several parts of the country have submerged vegetable and chilli fields, disrupted supplies and increased transportation costs. The seasonal decline in supply during the monsoon has also contributed to higher prices of most essential commodities.
Fish prices have risen by Tk20–30 per kg over the past week. Pangas is now selling at Tk250 per kg, telapia at Tk280, rui at Tk300–450, pabda at Tk350–400, shrimp at Tk800–1,400, tengra at Tk700, indigenous koi at Tk700–800 and shoal at Tk700 per kg. Prices of bhetki, mrigel, baim, shing and poa fish have also increased.
Hilsa is being sold at Tk1,600–3,200 per kg, depending on its size and quality, while prices of sea fish have also climbed beyond the reach of many middle- and low-income consumers.
Anwar Hossain, a fish vendor at Dhupkhola Kitchen Market, said adverse weather has kept many fishing trawlers from going to sea, while supplies from different parts of the country have declined.
"Wholesale prices have increased due to lower supply, and that has inevitably pushed up retail prices," he said.
Consumers say persistently high food prices are forcing them to rethink their spending, with fish and meat becoming increasingly unaffordable.
"My children wanted to eat fish, but I was shocked by the prices at the market," said shopper Jony Sheikh. "I somehow managed to buy one fish for them. If prices keep rising, we'll have to cut back on fish and meat."
Green chilli prices have surged to Tk400 per kg across Dhaka's kitchen markets, up by around Tk100 from a week ago. Retailers are charging Tk40 for 100 grams and Tk100 for 250 grams.
Locally produced onions have also become costlier, rising by Tk15–20 per kg over the past one-and-a-half to two weeks. Depending on quality, they are now selling for Tk55–65 per kg.
Vegetable prices remain high, with long brinjal selling for Tk120–150 per kg, round brinjal Tk180, white brinjal Tk140, bitter gourd Tk120–140, yardlong beans Tk110–130, snake gourd Tk90–100 and taro corms Tk80–100 per kg. Only sponge gourd and pointed gourd offered some relief, with prices easing to Tk60–80 per kg. Rafique, a vegetable vendor, blamed the price hike on supply shortages caused by heavy rains and flooding.
"Supplies from different parts of the country have declined during the monsoon, while waterlogging has damaged chilli fields in major producing areas. Reduced supply has pushed up prices," he said.
Sridevi Biswas, a shopper at Ray Saheb Bazar, said she had planned to buy several vegetables but returned home with only one.
"I came to buy a few vegetables, but after seeing the prices I bought only one. If this trend continues, it will become even harder for middle-income families to manage their household expenses," she said. Egg prices have also moved up, with farm eggs now selling for Tk145–155 per dozen, compared with Tk135–140 a week ago.
Poultry prices also increased over the past day. Broiler chicken is now selling for Tk190–200 per kg, up from Tk180, while Sonali chicken has risen to Tk340–350 per kg from Tk330–340.
Robin Hasan, a university student living in a shared accommodation, said eggs and chicken had long been the most affordable protein options.
"Even those are becoming more expensive now. Managing within a limited budget is getting harder every day," he said.
While prices of coarse, medium-grade and Miniket rice have remained largely stable, polao rice has seen a sharp spike.
Coarse rice is selling for Tk58–65 per kg, medium-grade rice for Tk68–78, and Miniket and Nazirshail varieties for Tk80–95 per kg.
In contrast, polao rice, which sold for Tk120–140 per kg just a few days ago, is now priced at Tk180–200 per kg, marking an increase of Tk50–60 per kg.
Traders said the jump is the steepest increase in the rice market in recent weeks, adding to the financial strain on consumers already grappling with the rising cost of living.
